title: Assam: Five killed as van collides with truck in Sonitpur
teaser: Five people were killed in Assam’s Sonitpur after an Eeco van collided head-on with a truck on NH-15 late Friday night. The truck driver is missing.
description: Five people were killed in Assam’s Sonitpur after an Eeco van collided head-on with a truck on NH-15 late Friday night. The truck driver is missing.
content: Five people were killed in Assam’s Sonitpur district after their vehicle collided head-on with a truck on National Highway 15 late Friday night, police said on Saturday. The accident took place in the Balipara area at around 11:30pm on Friday. The truck driver is yet to be traced, police officers said. “The incident was reported at around 11:30pm and a police team went to the spot where they found five critically injured men. They were taken to a nearby government hospital where two of them were declared dead on arrival while three others succumbed during treatment,” senior superintendent of police (SSP) of Sonitpur, Barun Purkayastha, said. Police have identified the deceased as Harobinda Hazoary (38), Pranjal Bania (39), Sanjay Mech (39), Papu Borah (45) and Nayan Swargiary (45), all of them residents of Batabari. They were travelling from Tezpur town to Rangapara in a Maruti Suzuki Eeco van and the truck was coming from the opposite direction when the two vehicles collided, police officers said. “We are trying to find the reason behind the collision but initial investigation suggests that the Eeco van lost control and crossed into the opposite lane before hitting the truck. The driver of the truck has been missing,” an officer said. Locals who witnessed the accident said that both the vehicles were at high speed and the Eeco van entered the opposite lane after losing control, and the impact of the collision was massive. “The sound was massive and it was heard from our houses,” a local who informed the police said. Police have taken both vehicles into custody and sent the five bodies to Sonitpur Civil Hospital for postmortem. The Assam government has been promoting road safety measures and, according to chief minister Himanta Biswa Sarma, the number of fatalities has decreased in recent years. However, according to the state government, nearly 4,000 road accidents have been reported in the state this year so far, and the number of deaths is in the hundreds.

title: who-is-cai-qi-xi-jinping-right-hand-brics
teaser: Discover why Cai Qi, China's second-most powerful leader and Xi Jinping's right hand, accompanied the Chinese President to India for the BRICS Summit.
description: Discover why Cai Qi, China's second-most powerful leader and Xi Jinping's right hand, accompanied the Chinese President to India for the BRICS Summit.
content: President of China Xi Jinping traveled to India's capital, New Delhi, for the upcoming BRICS Summit, accompanied by Cai Qi, head of the General Office of the Communist Party of China (CPC), who is considered the second most powerful political figure in Beijing's government structure. His presence alongside Xi represents an unprecedented concentration of administrative powers and proven political loyalty at the top level of the Chinese state administration. Cai Qi managed to accelerate significantly his career path in the Chinese Communist Party, thus overcoming the traditional bureaucratic timelines of promotions. Breakneck access to Politburo: In 2017, Cai became appointed as a member of the ruling Politburo, which is the second-highest decision-making body in China, shortly after taking up the post of Communist Party chief in Beijing. Norm-defying promotion: Prior to becoming the leader of the Politburo, Cai served as Beijing's mayor; however, he has bypassed the standard five-year transitional timeline expected for such a move. Standing committee peak: By 2022, Cai had secured his place atop the pinnacle of state power by joining the seven-member Politburo Standing Committee, the pinnacle of China’s political power circles. Cai's remit includes ideological training, schedule planning, and control over the machinery of the party’s center. Chief of Staff responsibilities: As the head of the CPC General Office, Cai operates as the operational chief of staff for Xi Jinping, managing core access and administrative processes. Ideological control: During his first months as a top-level official, Cai became the leader of the Central Party School, the elite educational institution responsible for the development of official ideology and training of young bureaucrats. Diplomacy: Moving out of the shadows of administration, Cai took up roles in diplomacy and welcomed international officials and received foreign delegations in important international summits. The basis for Cai’s power lies in decades-long political background and similar experiences of the supreme leader of China. Formative periods: Both Xi and Cai have gone through the turbulent periods of the Cultural Revolution as worker-peasant-soldier students in their formative years. Coastal alliances: Their professional partnership deepened over two decades of service in China's eastern coastal provinces of Fujian and Zhejiang, forging a trusted alliance that endured through decades of leadership transitions. Strategic signaling: By bringing his most trusted administrative enforcer to New Delhi, Xi underscored the strategic weight Beijing places on repairing diplomatic and economic engagements with India. Strategic signaling: By bringing his most trusted administrative enforcer to New Delhi, Xi underscored the strategic weight Beijing places on repairing diplomatic and economic engagements with India. title: Iowa County’s wind turbines turn into $2.71 million for roads, bridges and schools
teaser: In Howard County, wind turbines have emerged as a significant revenue stream for public finances. The impressive $2.7 million generated in tax revenue supports vital infrastructure, such as bridges and roads, as well as local educational in
description: In Howard County, wind turbines have emerged as a significant revenue stream for public finances. The impressive $2.7 million generated in tax revenue supports vital infrastructure, such as bridges and roads, as well as local educational in
content: When wind turbines first appeared across Howard County in northeastern Iowa in 2008, they became part of the rural landscape. Nearly two decades later, the towering structures have become something more than a source of renewable energy. For the county, wind power has also become a major source of public money, helping pay for bridges, roads, parks, conservation projects and local schools.A 2025 case study by the Centre for Rural Affairs found that Howard County had 147 wind turbines with a combined production capacity of 244 megawatts. In the 2024-25 tax year, the turbines generated $2.71 million in tax revenue, accounting for about 14.5% of the county's overall revenue.The money has been particularly significant for a rural county with a relatively small and declining population. Howard County had 9,469 residents in 2020, down from 9,566 in 2010, even as Iowa's overall population grew by about 5% during the same period. With limited population growth and a largely stagnant tax base, officials said the additional revenue from wind projects has helped the county maintain infrastructure without placing the same burden on residents.From wind farms to bridges and roadsThe first wind projects in Howard County were the Pioneer I and II developments, whose turbines were erected in 2008 and 2009. The projects installed 182 turbines, producing 178 MW of capacity, across the northwest corner of Howard County and the northeast corner of neighbouring Mitchell County.In 2019, Madison Gas and Electric added another 33 turbines, with 66 MW of capacity, around 12 miles west of Cresco, the Howard County seat. The Centre for Rural Affairs' county-level tally puts the number of turbines within Howard County at 147.The county used a financing mechanism known as Tax Increment Financing, or TIF, to channel much of the wind-related tax revenue into infrastructure and other public projects. TIF essentially allows governments to use increases in property-tax revenue associated with new development to finance community improvements. In Howard County, the system was used to fund $21.5 million worth of special projects without an additional cost to local residents, according to the case study. The largest share went into roads and bridges.Wind-related TIF money funded 30 bridge replacements involving bridges longer than 20 feet, a portion of four bridge rehabilitations and two smaller bridge replacements. Together, bridge projects received about $6.5 million. Another $12 million went toward roads, including 20 miles of paving and eight miles of grading.The Iowa Legislature's 2024-25 annual urban renewal report also shows that Howard County maintains a dedicated Wind Urban Renewal Area. The report says its purpose includes improvements to road shoulders, bridges, approaches, culverts and conservation projects in parks. It recorded $1.29 million in TIF revenue for the area during the fiscal year, with more than $1 million spent through the wind-farm TIF programme.‘We would have been forced to close’ bridgesThe impact is particularly visible in the county's bridge network. Howard County Engineer Nick Rissman told researchers that without the wind-turbine funding, officials would have faced difficult choices over which bridges to maintain.The additional money allowed the county to double the number of bridge projects it completed between 2010 and 2020 compared with the previous decade, according to the case study. More than 30 bridge projects were fully paid for through the wind-related funding without increasing taxes on residents.The benefit also extended beyond individual projects. About $1.5 million went toward equipment, including portions of the cost of six motor graders, a tractor with a mower and a dump truck.Rissman described the effect as a “snowball” process. By completing road projects earlier and purchasing equipment, the county could take on additional work instead of allowing roads to deteriorate until they required more expensive repairs.Parks, conservation and schools also benefitThe wind revenue did not stop at transportation infrastructure. The county allocated another $1.5 million to recreation and conservation projects. These included renovations at local parks, improvements at a nature centre, dam repairs, watershed projects and fishing habitat.Lake Hendricks Park, for example, received funding for fishing structures, watershed improvements and road paving. Money also went toward renovations at Florenceville Park, Lylah's Marsh Park, Vernon Springs Park and Lidtke Park, as well as improvements at the Bonair shooting range. The Prairie Springs and Wapsi Great Western Line recreational trails also received funding for repaving.Local schools have benefited as well. Wind projects provided an additional $228,071 annually to the Riceville Community School District and Howard-Winneshiek Community School District. The money can support school grounds and buildings, equipment and technology, transportation and other expenses.The wind development also contributes to the taxable property base of the school districts. The case study noted that Riceville's school district had the third-lowest total general tax rate among Iowa's 334 school districts, partly because of the high taxable valuation created by wind turbines.Farmers get another source of incomeThe financial impact is not limited to government coffers. Farmers who host turbines receive payments through land-lease agreements with wind-energy developers. Several Howard County landowners interviewed for the study said the additional income had helped them reinvest in their farms, including purchasing machinery, building sheds and improving their properties.The experience has not been without challenges. County officials said wind developers must take responsibility for damage caused to local roads during construction, while farmers stressed the importance of carefully negotiated lease agreements.Still, Howard County's experience offers a striking example of how a renewable-energy project can have effects far beyond electricity generation. The turbines standing in Iowa's fields are producing power, but their financial footprint can be seen elsewhere too: in newly paved roads, repaired bridges, upgraded parks, better-equipped schools and farm operations receiving another stream of income. For a rural county facing a limited tax base and little population growth, the wind has effectively become a source of infrastructure funding.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. title: NIA raids seven locations across Kashmir in Lashkar-e-Taiba terror probe
teaser: NIA searches seven locations in Kashmir in connection with a Lashkar-e-Taiba cross-border terror conspiracy case involving local support networks.
description: NIA searches seven locations in Kashmir in connection with a Lashkar-e-Taiba cross-border terror conspiracy case involving local support networks.
content: The National Investigation Agency searched seven residential premises across the Kashmir Valley on Saturday. Security teams targeted locations in south and north Kashmir to investigate a Lashkar-e-Taiba cross-border terror network. The case involves Pakistan-based handlers and local facilitators who helped smuggle weapons and explosives across the border. Officials carried out search operations at two locations in Kulgam district, three in Bandipora district, and two in the Sopore area of Baramulla district. Officers from the agency worked alongside local police and security forces to search homes linked to the investigation. Officers stated that the probe is still active and more details will emerge as teams examine recovered materials. The case began on March 31, 2026, when local police stopped a motorcyclist during a late-night checkpoint operation near Zakoora in Srinagar. Officers recovered a hand grenade and live ammunition from the rider, who was identified as a local worker for Lashkar-e-Taiba. Police registered initial charges before the central agency took over the case as RC-02/2026/NIA/JMU, applying counter-terrorism, arms, and explosive laws. Investigators found evidence of a wider network managed by Pakistan-based handlers who used local helpers in the valley. These local helpers provided shelter, transport, communication tools, and information about security movements to infiltrated terrorists. Authorities have already arrested Pakistani nationals linked to the scheme and mapped out the roles of local facilitators to dismantle the support structure. Syed Khalid Hussain is an award-winning journalist from Jammu & Kashmir with over 24 years of experience. He is currently working as Chief Special Correspondent at Zee Media. He has extensively covered the Kashmir conflict for nearly two decades while reporting from across India Delhi, Jammu, Ladakh and Punjab.

source_text: The National Investigation Agency searched seven residential premises across the Kashmir Valley on Saturday. Security teams targeted locations in south and north Kashmir to investigate a Lashkar-e-Taiba cross-border terror network. The case involves Pakistan-based handlers and local facilitators who helped smuggle weapons and explosives across the border. Officials carried out search operations at two locations in Kulgam district, three in Bandipora district, and two in the Sopore area of Baramulla district. Officers from the agency worked alongside local police and security forces to search homes linked to the investigation. Officers stated that the probe is still active and more details will emerge as teams examine recovered materials. The case began on March 31, 2026, when local police stopped a motorcyclist during a late-night checkpoint operation near Zakoora in Srinagar. Officers recovered a hand grenade and live ammunition from the rider, who was identified as a local worker for Lashkar-e-Taiba. Police registered initial charges before the central agency took over the case as RC-02/2026/NIA/JMU, applying counter-terrorism, arms, and explosive laws. Investigators found evidence of a wider network managed by Pakistan-based handlers who used local helpers in the valley. These local helpers provided shelter, transport, communication tools, and information about security movements to infiltrated terrorists. Authorities have already arrested Pakistani nationals linked to the scheme and mapped out the roles of local facilitators to dismantle the support structure. title: The ghost Limo of the BRICS Summit: Inside the armor and mystery of Xi Jinping`s Hongqi N701
teaser: Know why Chinese President Xi Jinping’s Hongqi N701 limousine arrived in Delhi under heavy black covers for the BRICS summit, and explore its secret security features.
description: Know why Chinese President Xi Jinping’s Hongqi N701 limousine arrived in Delhi under heavy black covers for the BRICS summit, and explore its secret security features.
content: Chinese President Xi Jinping’s arrival at the BRICS summit in New Delhi sparked viral intrigue after his official convoy vehicles were spotted being transported across the capital under heavy black covers. At the center of the mystery is the Hongqi N701, a highly secretive, heavily armored state limousine specifically engineered for China’s top leadership. Transporting presidential vehicles under wraps is standard protocol for high-security overseas state visits, designed to protect the asset from damage and limit unnecessary technical scrutiny during transit. Covering executive transport vehicles during international deployment serves precise logistical and security functions. Transit protection: Heavy-duty tarpaulins shield luxury finishes from dust, severe weather, and transit damage while being unloaded from cargo aircraft or moved on flatbed carriers. Scrutiny limitations: Concealing the vehicle during logistics phases prevents unauthorized close-up photographs, measurements, and security assessments before the car is officially deployed. Standard protocol: The tarps seen across Delhi roads reflect routine advance-team preparations rather than any reactive security measure following Xi's touchdown. Manufactured by China's historic luxury marque Hongqi—translating directly to “Red Flag”—the N701 is an exclusive vehicle unavailable to the general public. Imposing dimensions: Measuring approximately 5.5 meters (18 feet) in length, the sedan commands an intimidating road presence highlighted by a signature cascading grille and emblem. Classified armor: While official specifications remain strictly confidential, reports indicate the limousine features multi-hit ballistic glass, reinforced bodywork, and run-flat protected tires. Powertrain capabilities: Industry estimates suggest the vehicle is powered by a massive 6.0-liter V12 engine churning out roughly 408 horsepower, though exact performance metrics remain under wraps. The Hongqi N701 has previously accompanied Xi on high-profile international tours to regions like Russia, the United States, Hong Kong, and Egypt. Domestic pride: Utilising an indigenous marque highlights Beijing's policy of relying on domestic industrial power rather than foreign luxury manufacturers for top-tier leadership transport. Aurus Senat comparison: Xi's Hongqi is not the only high-security fortress roaming Delhi during the summit, as Russian President Vladimir Putin brought his own bespoke, heavily armored Aurus Senat limousine. title: Delhi High Court bars misuse of AI deepfakes infringing Rajat Sharma’s personality rights
teaser: The Delhi High Court has permanently barred various online video channels, individuals and online entities (defendants) from circulating deepfake videos and images of journalist Rajat Sharma and India TV and misusing Sharma’s personality at
description: The Delhi High Court has permanently barred various online video channels, individuals and online entities (defendants) from circulating deepfake videos and images of journalist Rajat Sharma and India TV and misusing Sharma’s personality at
content: The Delhi High Court has permanently barred various online video channels, individuals and online entities (defendants) from circulating deepfake videos and images of journalist Rajat Sharma and India TV and misusing Sharma’s personality attributes [Rajat Sharma Vs Tamara Doc]. Justice Jyoti Singh restrained the defendants from infringing Sharma’s personality and publicity rights as well as India TV’s intellectual property rights. The order was passed on August 24. Sharma and India TV had approached the Court seeking protection against infringement of his personality and publicity rights, infringement of India TV’s registered trademarks, misappropriation of goodwill, unfair trade practices and copyright violations. They alleged that several defendants were spreading misinformation through artificial intelligence-generated doctored videos containing distorted and modified images, voices and other personality traits of Sharma. They also alleged unauthorised use of India TV’s registered trademarks and violation of its copyright. In December 2024, the High Court had passed an ex parte interim order restraining several defendants from infringing Sharma’s personality and publicity rights and India TV’s intellectual property. Meta was then directed to block or remove the impugned content and disclose details of the concerned defendants. The Department of Telecommunications and the Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology were also directed to facilitate the blocking of infringing websites, telephone numbers, social-media accounts and channels. During the pendency of the suit, four YouTube channels were made party to the case after they were accused of circulating deepfake videos using Sharma’s personality attributes. In November 2025, Google was directed to take down some of these YouTube channels and disclose available subscriber information, IP logs and other account details. The defendants, against whom the suit was eventually decreed, had been served but failed to file written statements. Their right to do so was closed by the Joint Registrar in July 2026. The Court also gave Sharma and India TV liberty to directly approach Meta and Google with details of any fresh URLs or content involving misuse of Sharma’s name, likeness, image, voice, photographs or videos. The platforms have to acknowledge such requests within 24 hours and take action within 36 hours thereafter, after independently examining the complaint under their respective policies. Sharma can approach the Court again if no action is taken. India TV was also given liberty to seek a declaration in a subsequent suit that its trademarks are “well-known” marks under the Trade Marks Act. Sharma and India TV were represented by advocates Sidharth Chopra, Disha Sharma, Snehima Jauhari and Deepika Pokharia from Saikrishna & Associates. Google was represented by advocates Aditya Gupta, Vani Kaushik and Rohith Venkatesan. The Union government authorities were represented by Central Government Standing Counsel Nishant Gautam along with advocates Manish Rawat, Srishti Singh, Mohit Bokoliya and Abhishek Mohanpuria. title: Law, music and cinema not strangers to each other: Supreme Court Justice V Mohana at NUALS seminar
teaser: Supreme Court Justice V Mohana on Friday drew parallels between law, music and cinema observing that all three involve interpretation and making sense of human experiences within their respective frameworks.Drawing a parallel between music
description: Supreme Court Justice V Mohana on Friday drew parallels between law, music and cinema observing that all three involve interpretation and making sense of human experiences within their respective frameworks.Drawing a parallel between music
content: Supreme Court Justice V Mohana on Friday drew parallels between law, music and cinema observing that all three involve interpretation and making sense of human experiences within their respective frameworks. Drawing a parallel between music and law, the judge said that while music has rules, rhythm structure and harmony which help an artist create music, so does law which has Constitution, legislation and procedure which provides a framework within which judges and lawyers work. "Law is not entirely different, the Constitution, legislation and procedure give us our framework, they tell us where the boundaries are and so judges are constantly trying to do something quite delicate; to interpret law faithfully while recognising that the world in which the law operates is constantly changing. The answer to why art matters to law is rather simple. We spend a great deal of time in law dealing with categories, principles and procedures. But behind every case is a person, behind every legal dispute is a human experience," Justice Mohana said. She was speaking at the inaugural ceremony of the 'Three-day Seminar on Music, Cinema and Law: Exploring the Intersections of Art, Culture and Law,' jointly organised by the Kerala Judicial Academy and the National University of Advanced Studies (NUALs) at Bolgatty in Kochi. The seminar was inaugurated by Kerala Chief Minister VD Satheesan in the presence of Justice Mohana, Kerala High Court Chief Justice Soumen Sen, Justice Anil K Narendran, Minister of Higher Education Roji M John, other judges, lawyers, academics and members of the creative community. The inaugural ceremony was preceded by 'Navarasa', a classical dance presentation by Kerala Kalamandalam. At the outset, the Justice Mohana said that she had initially wondered what a judge could say about music and cinema, but as she thought more about the theme of the seminar, she found that the three seemingly different fields had much in common. "The more I thought about law, music and cinema, more I realized that perhaps these three words are not strangers to each other. There is actually something very familiar about law, music and cinema," Justice Mohana stated. She also spoke about the emergence and impact of Artificial Intelligence (AI) on artists and creative industry. "Today, this relationship between art and law is becoming even more complicated. Your voice can be copied, your face can be recreated. Music can be generated by a machine, and actors can appear on screen without having performed a scene. Law is being asked questions that were the most unimaginable even a few years ago. Where does inspiration end and imitation begin? When does technology assist an artist, and when does it replace one?" She said that answers to such fundamentally new questions concerning creativity, imitation and ownership cannot come from the legal fraternity alone. Justice Mohana stressed that artists, musicians, filmmakers, technologists, historians and academics must come together to understand the challenges and find solutions to protect creativity while allowing innovation to progress. Before concluding her speech, Justice Mohana urged the judges, lawyers, artists and academics participating in the seminar to use the event and understand perspectives beyond their own fields. She said that they should not only speak about issues relating to law and art from their professional viewpoints but also listen to how other disciplines understand and approach the same challenges. "I hope that when we leave from here, we will have understood not only what law can say to music and cinema, but also what music and cinema can teach law," she concluded. Chief Minister VD Satheesan highlighted the growing challenges that new technologies pose to the rights of artist and creators. Referring particularly to AI, Satheesan questioned how law would deal with creative works generated using such technology and added that the legal framework should evolve alongside the advancements in order to address the emerging challenges. "We are all saying about law - that law is living law, law is changing time to time. I hope that after the introduction of this future technology, there should be many changes in the legal framework also. For example, this copyright, intellectual property right, the piracy thing, everything there should be a change," he said Chief Justice Soumen Sen drew parallels between the role of a musician interpreting a composition and that of a judge interpreting a legal text. "A musical score does not perform itself. The musician must remain faithful to the composition, but must also bring phrasing, emphasis, dynamism and sensitivity. A legal text presents a similar challenge. The judge is neither a mechanical reproducer of words nor an unfettered creator. Interpretation requires fidelity to the text, but also an understanding of context, structure and purpose," he said. Justice Anil K Narendran also highlighted the impact of AI and stressed that it is necessary to examine whether the existing legal framework adequately protects creative works and artist rights, while ensuring that the technological progress does not hinder or exploit human creativity. "We cannot and should not approach Artificial Intelligence as a threat or assume that it will not be a permitted development. The challenge before us is how the law can ensure that this progress does not come at the cost of human creativity," said Justice Narendran. Copyright © 2021 Bar and Bench. All Rights Reserved

Before concluding her speech, Justice Mohana urged the judges, lawyers, artists and academics participating in the seminar to use the event and understand perspectives beyond their own fields. She said that they should not only speak about issues relating to law and art from their professional viewpoints but also listen to how other disciplines understand and approach the same challenges. "I hope that when we leave from here, we will have understood not only what law can say to music and cinema, but also what music and cinema can teach law," she concluded. Chief Minister VD Satheesan highlighted the growing challenges that new technologies pose to the rights of artist and creators. Referring particularly to AI, Satheesan questioned how law would deal with creative works generated using such technology and added that the legal framework should evolve alongside the advancements in order to address the emerging challenges. "We are all saying about law - that law is living law, law is changing time to time. I hope that after the introduction of this future technology, there should be many changes in the legal framework also. For example, this copyright, intellectual property right, the piracy thing, everything there should be a change," he said Chief Justice Soumen Sen drew parallels between the role of a musician interpreting a composition and that of a judge interpreting a legal text. "A musical score does not perform itself. The musician must remain faithful to the composition, but must also bring phrasing, emphasis, dynamism and sensitivity. A legal text presents a similar challenge. The judge is neither a mechanical reproducer of words nor an unfettered creator. Interpretation requires fidelity to the text, but also an understanding of context, structure and purpose," he said. The challenge before us is how the law can ensure that this progress does not come at the cost of human creativity," said Justice Narendran. Copyright © 2021 Bar and Bench. All Rights Reserved

title: Command in the clouds: How Xi Jinping`s modified Boeing 747-8 serves as a mobile HQ at the BRICS Summit
teaser: Know the specifications, security systems, and command capabilities of Chinese President Xi Jinping's modified Boeing 747-8 presidential aircraft.
description: Know the specifications, security systems, and command capabilities of Chinese President Xi Jinping's modified Boeing 747-8 presidential aircraft.
content: Chinese President Xi Jinping travels internationally aboard a heavily modified Boeing 747-8 operated by Air China under a dedicated VVIP configuration. Unlike the United States' permanently commissioned Air Force One fleet, Beijing utilizes commercial airframes converted for state duties, combining long-range intercontinental capability with mobile command infrastructure. Registered as B-2479 and deployed during major state tours like the Delhi BRICS summit, the aircraft serves as a secure, flying command center for the nation's leadership. The Boeing 747-8 is a wide-body, four-engine commercial airframe adapted for elite diplomatic deployment. Dimensions and range: Stretching nearly 76 meters in length with a 68-meter wingspan, the four-engine jet achieves a non-stop intercontinental range exceeding 14,000 kilometers. Powerplant performance: Powered by four General Electric GEnx-2B67 engines generating approximately 66,500 pounds of thrust each, the aircraft cruises at Mach 0.855. Interior configuration: Passenger capacity is radically reduced compared to commercial variants, making room for a private presidential suite, executive meeting rooms, secure briefing offices, and onboard medical facilities. Military-grade defence and secure communication systems The presidential transport is outfitted with advanced defense architecture designed to maintain continuity of government under extreme threat scenarios. Countermeasure suites: The aircraft features integrated missile warning sensors and automated countermeasure deployment systems to deflect incoming projectiles. EMP hardening: Electromagnetic pulse (EMP) shielding protects onboard digital avionics and communication arrays from nuclear or electronic disruption. Encrypted Command Hubs: Secure satellite communication links allow the president to manage state and military affairs continuously from mid-air. Different geopolitical powers utilize distinct strategic models for their executive air transport fleets. US Air Force One: Based on heavily modified Boeing airframes, American presidential aircraft feature dedicated military crews, aerial refueling capabilities, and extensive open security layouts. Russia's flying Kremlin: Vladimir Putin travels via the Ilyushin Il-96-300PU, a four-engine, domestically engineered wide-body aircraft prioritizing Russian aviation tech. Air India One: India’s Prime Minister utilises a modified Boeing 777-300ER operated by the Indian Air Force, featuring advanced defense integration and long-haul twin-engine efficiency. title: Xi Jinping in India after 7 years, set to meet Narendra Modi today
teaser: Xi Jinping arrived in India for the Brics Summit after seven years and is set to meet Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Saturday amid efforts to normalise ties.
description: Xi Jinping arrived in India for the Brics Summit after seven years and is set to meet Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Saturday amid efforts to normalise ties.
content: Chinese President Xi Jinping travelled to India on Saturday for the first time in seven years to attend the Brics Summit, setting the stage for bilateral talks with Prime Minister Narendra Modi to advance the normalisation of ties amid lingering tensions on the border. Xi, who last visited the Indian capital in 2014, was received at the airport by minister of state for commerce Jitin Prasada. External affairs ministry spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal said India looks forward to constructive discussions with China as Brics advances cooperation and contributes to a more balanced, representative and multipolar world. The leaders of India and China have not made any bilateral visits since 2020, when relations plummeted to their lowest point since the 1962 border war because of a face-off between troops of the two sides in Ladakh. Xi last travelled to India in 2019 for an informal summit with Modi, months before the standoff began and continued for more than four years. Xi and Modi are set to meet on Saturday evening to assess the progress made by the two sides in addressing the dragging border dispute and normalising bilateral ties since they reached an understanding in October 2024 on disengagement of troops at all “friction points” in Ladakh sector of the Line of Actual Control (LAC). Even as the process of de-escalation and withdrawal of troops to peacetime locations in Ladakh sector remains incomplete, fresh tensions emerged in the Arunachal Pradesh sector after face-offs between troops during July and August. The talks between Xi and Modi will be an opportunity to take stock of several rounds of dialogue between the Special Representatives on the border issue, the Working Mechanism for Consultation and Coordination (WMCC) and senior military commanders. India and China held the first round of talks between military commanders in the eastern sector on September 6 and 7. People familiar with the matter said the Indian side is also expected to raise a range of concerns, including China’s visa curbs for Indian businesspeople, export restrictions on critical machinery and commodities such as fertilisers, and the yawning imbalance in two-way trade. Since Xi’s last visit, India-China trade has grown from about $93 billion in 2019 to $127 billion in 2025, while India’s trade deficit has risen from $57 billion to almost $100 billion in the same period. The two sides, however, have made progress in resuming direct flights, reviving the Kailash Mansarovar Yatra and restarting border trade through three designated points. Rezaul Hasan Laskar is Foreign Editor with the Hindustan Times, which he joined in 2015. He began as a journalist in his hometown of Shillong in northeast India and has worked in newspapers and wire services over the years. He moved to New Delhi in 1997 and initially focused on defence, national security, Jammu and Kashmir and the northeast, while also working of foreign policy and international relations. He has been part of the media delegation accompanying PMs on foreign visits and has reported from destinations ranging from Tibet to Ukraine. Between 2007 and 2013, he was the Press Trust of India correspondent in Pakistan, one of only two Indian journalists allowed to report from the country. He extensively covered Pakistan’s domestic politics and the life of the common people, as well as the fallout of the 2008 Mumbai attacks on India-Pakistan relations and the subsequent trial in Pakistan of the suspects involved in the attack. As part of his reportage in Pakistan, he travelled the breadth of the country, from the Swat Valley to Balochistan. Reza’s first gig in journalism was writing a weekly music column, and music – especially classic rock – remains a keen interest. He is also a movie buff and a keen photographer. Read More

source_text: Chinese President Xi Jinping travelled to India on Saturday for the first time in seven years to attend the Brics Summit, setting the stage for bilateral talks with Prime Minister Narendra Modi to advance the normalisation of ties amid lingering tensions on the border. Xi, who last visited the Indian capital in 2014, was received at the airport by minister of state for commerce Jitin Prasada. External affairs ministry spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal said India looks forward to constructive discussions with China as Brics advances cooperation and contributes to a more balanced, representative and multipolar world. The leaders of India and China have not made any bilateral visits since 2020, when relations plummeted to their lowest point since the 1962 border war because of a face-off between troops of the two sides in Ladakh. Xi last travelled to India in 2019 for an informal summit with Modi, months before the standoff began and continued for more than four years. Xi and Modi are set to meet on Saturday evening to assess the progress made by the two sides in addressing the dragging border dispute and normalising bilateral ties since they reached an understanding in October 2024 on disengagement of troops at all “friction points” in Ladakh sector of the Line of Actual Control (LAC). Even as the process of de-escalation and withdrawal of troops to peacetime locations in Ladakh sector remains incomplete, fresh tensions emerged in the Arunachal Pradesh sector after face-offs between troops during July and August. The talks between Xi and Modi will be an opportunity to take stock of several rounds of dialogue between the Special Representatives on the border issue, the Working Mechanism for Consultation and Coordination (WMCC) and senior military commanders. India and China held the first round of talks between military commanders in the eastern sector on September 6 and 7. People familiar with the matter said the Indian side is also expected to raise a range of concerns, including China’s visa curbs for Indian businesspeople, export restrictions on critical machinery and commodities such as fertilisers, and the yawning imbalance in two-way trade. Since Xi’s last visit, India-China trade has grown from about $93 billion in 2019 to $127 billion in 2025, while India’s trade deficit has risen from $57 billion to almost $100 billion in the same period. The two sides, however, have made progress in resuming direct flights, reviving the Kailash Mansarovar Yatra and restarting border trade through three designated points. title: Putin's 'Doomsday Plane' in Delhi: Why this luxurious, Soviet era aircraft is named so?
teaser: Putin’s “Flying Kremlin” has arrived in India for the BRICS Summit. Here’s what makes the presidential aircraft so unique and secure.
description: Putin’s “Flying Kremlin” has arrived in India for the BRICS Summit. Here’s what makes the presidential aircraft so unique and secure.
content: Russian president Vladimir Putin arrived in Delhi on September 11, for the 18th BRICS Summit aboard one of the most heavily guarded aircraft in the world— the specially modified Ilyushin Il-96-300PU, popularly known as the “Flying Kremlin” or, in some reports, Putin’s “Doomsday Plane”. Putin is in India for a three-day visit during which, he is holding talks with Prime Minister Narendra Modi and attending the BRICS summit. Vladimir Putin’s “Flying Kremlin”, also referred to as the "Doomsday Plane” is a modified version of the Ilyushin Il-96-300, a long-range, four-engine Russian airliner developed by the Ilyushin Design Bureau in the 1980s. With its roots in the Soviet era, the aircraft remains one of the most distinctive presidential jets in the world. The Il-96-300PU is not Russia’s dedicated “Doomsday Plane”. According to a report by OneIndia, that designation is generally associated with the Ilyushin Il-80, which was specifically developed as an airborne command post designed to maintain strategic command and control during a nuclear conflict or other major national emergency. The Il-96-300PU used by Putin is primarily a presidential command and transport aircraft. Its importance lies in allowing the Russian president to continue communicating securely while airborne, even during situations in which conventional communications could be compromised. Also Read | Xi Jinping's car arrives in Delhi under black covers. What we know about the 'secret' Hongqi N701 One of the most striking aspects of Putin’s aircraft arrangements is the use of two identical Il-96-300PU aircraft. According to a report by NDTV, both aircrafts were used during his journey to India, with the planes flying simultaneously. The tactic is intended to make it difficult for outsiders to determine which aircraft is carrying Putin. Both jets have a similar appearance, making the president’s exact location harder to identify. The Il-96-300PU combines the characteristics of a long-range presidential aircraft with those of a secure command centre. Its communications equipment is considered among its most important features, allowing the Russian leadership to maintain contact while travelling. Reports have also highlighted electronic countermeasures and other defensive systems aboard the aircraft, including radar-jamming technology and infrared countermeasures. However, details of its exact capabilities remain classified, and some claims about the aircraft’s defensive capabilities have not been independently verified. Also Read | Putin takes a dig at 'so-called' G7, stresses BRICS nations' 40% share of world GDP The Il-96-300PU is equipped with a private presidential suite featuring a bedroom, a spacious conference room with boardroom-style seating, a private office and a guest lounge. It also has dedicated dining and kitchen areas, along with a medical compartment. Some media reports have also claimed that the aircraft includes a fitness area to accommodate the president’s exercise routine. The cabin is finished with gold-plated accents, rich woodwork featuring rare Karelian birch, neoclassical furnishings, premium leather upholstery and ornate tapestries, giving the aircraft an opulent, mansion-like ambience rather than the feel of a conventional jet. Putin’s arrival has drawn attention during the BRICS Summit, where leaders of major emerging economies are meeting in New Delhi. His aircraft landed at Palam Air Force Station amid extensive security arrangements surrounding the Russian president’s visit. Also Read | Russia ready to contribute to global energy, food security, Putin pledges at BRICS The aircraft’s presence in India has therefore become a talking point in its own right — not simply because of its luxury or appearance, but because it represents the extraordinary level of security and communications infrastructure surrounding one of the world’s most closely protected leaders. title: ‘PM Modi is so popular’: Malaysian PM on Modi’s international appeal; Smriti Irani says ‘wave’ has ‘global echo’
teaser: PM Modi met his Malaysian counterpart Anwar Ibrahim on Saturday on the sidelines of the 18th BRICS Summit in Delhi.
description: PM Modi met his Malaysian counterpart Anwar Ibrahim on Saturday on the sidelines of the 18th BRICS Summit in Delhi.
content: Malaysian Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim, who is in India for the 18th BRICS Summit, met India's Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Saturday and candidly mentioned that he is so popular that people messaged him to pass on their regards to Modi. BJP leader Smriti Irani shared a video clip of the candid exchange and wrote: “The Modi wave has a global echo! Malaysian PM Mr. Anwar Ibrahim’s candid quip says it all...” Track live updates on BRICS Summit In the video, Ibrahim is seen shaking hands with PM Modi and as he proceeds to take a seat besides him, Ibrahim tells India's external affairs minister S Jaishankar that Modi is very popular. “I got so many messages to pass on regards to him,” Ibrahim can be heard saying. Also read: Xi Jinping's car arrives in Delhi under black covers. What we know about the 'secret' Hongqi N701 Modi on Saturday held talks with his Malaysian counterpart Anwar Ibrahim, focusing on boosting bilateral cooperation in sectors such as energy, defence, trade and investment. Also read: Ethiopia, Malaysia eye strong defence, business ties with India after Modi meet at BRICS "Building on Prime Minister Modi's visit to Malaysia in February 2026, the leaders reviewed the progress in bilateral cooperation across a range of areas, including trade and investment, defence and security, semiconductors, infrastructure, digital economy, energy, fintech, education, tourism and people-to-people ties," External Affairs Ministry spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal said on social media. The leaders exchanged views on key regional and global issues of mutual interest, he said. Ibrahim is among leaders of the global south who are in India for the 18th BRICS Summit on September 12 and 13 with focus on trade, investment and global conflicts, as the bloc seeks a bigger role in shaping the global agenda for emerging and developing countries. India is hosting Russian President Vladimir Putin, Chinese President Xi Jinping, Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian and counterparts from the other eight BRICS members. The summit comes as wars in Ukraine and the Middle East, along with rising U.S.-China tensions, test the bloc’s ability to find common ground among countries with competing geopolitical interests. Also read: BRICS 2026: PM Modi meets Abu Dhabi Crown Prince in Delhi; trade, energy security in focus BRICS, comprising Brazil, Russia, India, China and South Africa, expanded in 2024 to include Egypt, Ethiopia, Iran, the UAE and Saudi Arabia, with Indonesia joining in 2025. Belarus, Bolivia, Kazakhstan, Cuba, Malaysia, Nigeria, Thailand, Uganda, Uzbekistan and Vietnam became BRICS partner countries last year. title: Porn, movies found on seized phone, pen drive of jailed rape-convict Prajwal Revanna
teaser: The phone was among the items recovered during a surprise inspection at Bengaluru’s Parappana Agrahara Central Prison on August 11.
description: The phone was among the items recovered during a surprise inspection at Bengaluru’s Parappana Agrahara Central Prison on August 11.
content: Dozens of pornographic videos were allegedly found on the mobile phone seized from jailed former JD(S) MP Prajwal Revanna, latest forensic examination has revealed. The seized devices were subsequently sent for forensic analysis. The mobile phone contained several explicit videos, while a pen drive recovered during the search contained movies and web series, PTI reported. Revanna was allegedly found using an Android smartphone inside the prison last month. A video that surfaced later showed him in casual clothes speaking to someone on the phone. The phone and other devices were subsequently seized during a four-to-five-hour search by the Central Crime Branch (CCB) at his barrack. Also Read: Prison personnel among 7 held for supply of phone, SIM card to ex-MP Prajwal Revanna The investigation by the CEN police station found several dozen pornographic videos on the seized phone, the police officer told PTI. During questioning, however, Revanna denied owning the device and said other inmates used it and passed it around on a rotational basis. He also denied downloading any of the pornographic videos, the officer said. A notebook recovered during the search contained phone numbers belonging to Revanna's family members and acquaintances. Police said the call records showed unauthorised communication with family members through intermediaries, as well as direct calls to a female friend. Revanna reportedly acknowledged the latter during questioning. Police are expected to issue notices to people whose numbers appeared in the phone's call history. The prohibited mobile phone, SIM card, charger and notebook were recovered from a cell occupied by undertrial prisoner Prathap Rai and convicted former MP Revanna, according to police. A case was subsequently registered at Parappana Agrahara Police Station. Five people have been arrested in connection with the case, according to a police statement issued on Friday. Investigators said the accused had allegedly purchased the phone and SIM card and facilitated their entry into the prison. The accused allegedly told police that the phone was smuggled into the prison through a warder, while the SIM card was brought in through an undertrial prisoner. They also allegedly said the phone and SIM card were being used by Rai and Revanna. On September 8, Rai and Revanna were produced before a court and remanded to three days of police custody for questioning. They were sent back to prison on September 10 following a court order. title: Rare 1894 San Francisco dime sells for $1.25 million at auction
teaser: A rare 1894-S Barber dime has just sold for over one million dollars, reflecting its extraordinary scarcity. Out of the original twenty-four minted in San Francisco, only nine have survived to present day. This coin, steeped in historical i
description: A rare 1894-S Barber dime has just sold for over one million dollars, reflecting its extraordinary scarcity. Out of the original twenty-four minted in San Francisco, only nine have survived to present day. This coin, steeped in historical i
content: A 10-cent coin minted in San Francisco more than a century ago has just sold for about $1.25 million, turning one of the smallest denominations in US currency into a million-dollar collector's prize. The 1894-S Barber dime is one of the most famous rarities in American numismatics. According to auction house Stack's Bowers Galleries, which handled the recent sale, only 24 examples were struck in 1894 and just nine are known to survive today. The coin sold for $1,250,500 at the company's 2026 auction, more than 130 years after it was made.Why were only 24 dimes made?The extraordinary story of the 1894-S Barber dime begins at the San Francisco Mint during a period of economic difficulty. The United States was still dealing with the effects of the Panic of 1893, a severe financial crisis that contributed to a sharp reduction in demand for new coinage. Against that backdrop, just 24 Barber dimes were struck at the San Francisco Mint in June 1894. They were not ordinary coins produced in large quantities for everyday circulation. The tiny mintage eventually turned the dime into one of the great rarities of American coin collecting. The exact reason for the unusual production has never been established with complete certainty. According to evidence from the San Francisco Mint, a small quantity of subsidiary coin bullion remained after recoinage and was enough to produce 24 dimes. Another long-standing story says Mint Superintendent John Daggett had the coins struck for prominent banker friends and gave some to his daughter.The competing explanations are part of what has made the 1894-S dime so fascinating to collectors. Its rarity is certain; the circumstances surrounding its creation remain partly mysterious.A tiny coin with a famous designThe coin belongs to the Barber dime series, which was designed by Charles E. Barber, then chief engraver of the US Mint. The series was produced from 1892 to 1916. The obverse features Liberty wearing a cap, while the reverse carries the denomination "ONE DIME" inside a wreath. The small "S" mint mark on the reverse identifies the coin as having been produced at the San Francisco Mint.Although collectors can find Barber dimes from other years, the 1894-S issue is in a completely different category because of its extremely small mintage and tiny surviving population. Only nine examples are currently known to exist. That means every time one of these coins comes onto the market, collectors are competing for an object that almost never becomes available.From a 10-cent coin to a $1.25 million treasureThe latest sale demonstrates just how dramatically rarity can transform the value of an old coin. The 1894-S Barber dime that recently went under the hammer sold for $1,250,500 at Stack's Bowers Galleries on September 1, 2026. The latest sale is also part of a much longer history of extraordinary prices for the coin. One of the surviving dimes has changed hands for millions of dollars in previous years, with its value driven not simply by its age but by the combination of scarcity, historical mystery and collector demand.The 1894-S dime is particularly notable because its entire known population is small enough to make each specimen significant. A coin does not need to be thousands of years old to become extraordinarily valuable; in this case, a piece of American currency from the late 19th century has acquired a status approaching that of a national numismatic treasure.The dime that helped make Dave Bowers famousThe 1894-S dime also has an important connection to Dave Bowers, the legendary American numismatist and co-founder of Stack's Bowers Galleries. According to the auction house's history of the coin, Bowers purchased an 1894-S dime in 1957, when he was just 19 years old, for $4,750. At the time, spending thousands of dollars on a 10-cent coin was an extraordinary decision for a young collector.Bowers later sold the coin for $6,000. That early transaction became an important episode in his career and helped establish his reputation in the world of rare coins. The dime therefore became connected not only with American numismatic history but also with one of the most influential figures in the modern coin-collecting business.Why this dime remains legendaryThe appeal of the 1894-S Barber dime goes beyond its face value or even its silver content. Its story combines a mysterious origin, an exceptionally small mintage, a handful of surviving examples and decades of fascination among collectors. Of the original 24 coins, only nine are known today. That scarcity means that each surviving example represents a tiny piece of a production run that was never repeated.More than 130 years after the San Francisco Mint produced those 24 dimes, one of them has once again demonstrated why the coin is considered legendary. What began as a 10-cent piece in 1894 has become an object capable of commanding around $1.25 million at auction, showing how rarity and history can turn an ordinary denomination into one of the most coveted coins in American collecting.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. title: Naples estate returns at $195 million after $100 million price cut
teaser: Gordon Pointe, a Naples waterfront estate, is now listed for $195 million. This price represents a $100 million reduction from its initial listing. The property was assembled over decades by financier John Donahue. Its location offers exten
description: Gordon Pointe, a Naples waterfront estate, is now listed for $195 million. This price represents a $100 million reduction from its initial listing. The property was assembled over decades by financier John Donahue. Its location offers exten
content: A home once listed for a staggering $295 million is back on the market in Naples, Florida, but at a dramatically lower price. Gordon Pointe, the sprawling waterfront estate in the exclusive Port Royal neighbourhood, is now asking $195 million after being reduced and reshaped into a 5.39-acre offering. Realtor.com, which reported the latest listing, described the property as an iconic waterfront estate returning to the market after a $100 million price cut. Despite its extraordinary location, scale and private harbour, the estate has yet to find a buyer.From a $1 million purchase to a $295 million listingGordon Pointe has a remarkable history. Financier John Donahue began assembling the property in 1985, when he bought his first roughly four-acre waterfront parcel for about $1 million. Over the years, he expanded the family's holdings, eventually creating a much larger private compound. By 2024, the property had grown into a roughly nine-acre estate with multiple residences and extensive waterfront access. It was then placed on the market for $295 million, making it the most expensive home listing in the US at the time.The asking price reflected something that is almost impossible to recreate in Naples: an enormous private waterfront tract in one of the city's most desirable neighbourhoods. The property offers views of Naples Bay and the Gulf of Mexico, along with substantial beach frontage and a private yacht basin. Its scale and location were central to the sellers' argument that Gordon Pointe deserved a price far above that of a conventional luxury mansion.Why the property is now asking $195 millionThe estate's latest appearance on the market is somewhat different from its original offering. According to Realtor.com, Gordon Pointe has been reduced to a 5.39-acre property and is now listed for $195 million. It had most recently been offered for $210 million in January 2025 before returning to the market at the new price. Current property records show the listing at 100 & 104 Bay Road in Naples. The offering includes about 722 feet of beach frontage and a 231-foot yacht basin, with access to Naples Bay and views towards the Gulf.The reduction from $295 million to $195 million represents a $100 million drop, or roughly 34% from the original asking price. That does not mean the estate has suddenly become an ordinary luxury property. At $195 million, it remains one of the most expensive homes available in the country.What makes Gordon Pointe so valuable?For an ultra-wealthy buyer, the appeal is less about simply owning a large house and more about owning an irreplaceable piece of waterfront land. The property sits at the southern end of Gordon Drive in Port Royal. It combines privacy, direct beach frontage, boating access and views over both the bay and Gulf. The current listing describes the property as offering a protected harbour option through its yacht basin.The estate also has a history few properties can match. The Donahue family gradually assembled the land over decades, turning what began as a modest coastal property into a private compound. That history helps explain why the original asking price was so ambitious. Building a large mansion is possible; recreating a multi-acre waterfront holding in an established part of Naples is considerably harder.The hidden challenge: Florida's climate riskBut Gordon Pointe's extraordinary location also creates one of its biggest potential drawbacks. The property sits directly on the coast, making it exposed to hurricanes, storm surge and flooding. When the estate was still being offered for $295 million, flood-risk analysis by the First Street Foundation estimated a 68% chance of flooding within 15 years and 95% within 30 years. Climate-risk researchers also classified its exposure to wind as extreme.For most homeowners, those figures would be a major consideration. At the level of wealth required to purchase a $195 million property, the calculation can be different, but insurance and long-term maintenance can still become significant costs.Why hasn't someone bought it?The biggest obstacle may simply be the extremely small pool of people capable of purchasing it. At $195 million, Gordon Pointe is not competing with typical Naples homes. It is competing for the attention of a tiny group of ultra-high-net-worth buyers who want a very specific combination of privacy, waterfront access, land and prestige. The property also illustrates the difficulty of pricing trophy real estate. A seller can reduce an asking price by $100 million and still be left with a property that costs nearly $200 million.For the right buyer, however, that dramatic reduction could make Gordon Pointe considerably more compelling than it was when it carried a $295 million price tag. At $195 million, the estate remains an exceptionally rare waterfront property, offering a combination of land, privacy, beach frontage and boating access that is difficult to replicate in Naples. Whether that combination will be enough to attract a buyer remains to be seen.Ready to Make a Smarter Property Decision? Build Your Legacy with TOI Homes.

The property also illustrates the difficulty of pricing trophy real estate. A seller can reduce an asking price by $100 million and still be left with a property that costs nearly $200 million.For the right buyer, however, that dramatic reduction could make Gordon Pointe considerably more compelling than it was when it carried a $295 million price tag. At $195 million, the estate remains an exceptionally rare waterfront property, offering a combination of land, privacy, beach frontage and boating access that is difficult to replicate in Naples. Whether that combination will be enough to attract a buyer remains to be seen.Ready to Make a Smarter Property Decision? Build Your Legacy with TOI Homes.

title: China’s Air Force One: Inside Xi Jinping’s Boeing 747-8 Presidential Jet
teaser: China's presidential transport utilizes a specially converted Boeing 747-8I aircraft. This aircraft is branded with Air China and carries specific registration details. Several other nations also employ VIP-configured 747-8I models for thei
description: China's presidential transport utilizes a specially converted Boeing 747-8I aircraft. This aircraft is branded with Air China and carries specific registration details. Several other nations also employ VIP-configured 747-8I models for thei
content: While much of the world is familiar with America's Air Force One, China's presidential transport arrangements remain far less known, even though they are based on the same variant of the iconic Boeing-747. Air travel for China's top leadership—the CCP General Secretary, President, Premier and other senior officials —is managed by the 34th Division of the People's Liberation Army Air Force, which operates a fleet including six Boeing 737-300s, two 737-700s, four 737-800s, three Airbus A319s and ten Bombardier Challenger 800s. Notably, Chinese regulations restrict the use of dedicated presidential aircraft strictly to the President and the State Council Premier for international visits, other state leaders are required to use chartered planes instead.For Xi Jinping's own long-haul international travel, the aircraft of choice has been a specially converted Boeing 747-8I, carrying Air China branding and registration B-2479, converted and tested around 2016-2017 for exclusive head-of-state use. While no official photographs have ever been released, the aircraft is widely believed to be fitted with conference tables, private bedrooms and office suites—features expected of any long-range VIP transport. In the past, China has also used converted commercial Air China Boeing 747-400 aircraft for international travel when required, with three such aircraft carrying the registrations B-2445, B-2447 and B-2472.The Boeing 747-8, the aircraft at the heart of this fleet, is the final and largest member of the 747 family ever built, stretched to 250 feet in length, making it the longest airliner in commercial service. It features a deeper, thicker wing for greater fuel capacity, larger raked wingtips for improved aerodynamics, and more efficient GENx engines borrowed from the 787 Dreamliner, pushing its maximum takeoff weight to nearly 975,000 pounds, the heaviest of any Boeing airliner.China isn't the only nation to have turned to this aircraft for head-of-state duties. VIP-configured 747-8Is have also gone to Qatar, Kuwait, Oman, Brunei, Morocco, Turkey and Saudi Arabia, the last of which is used by Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman. Interestingly, the United States itself has recently adopted a version of the same aircraft, designated the VC-25B Bridge, a stopgap presidential transport built from a former Qatari VIP jet gifted to Washington in 2025, now used by President Trump while the definitive VC-25A replacements remain under development.India, Japan, Israel, Indonesia, Singapore, Bangladesh, South Africa and a few other nations use variants of the more modern Boeing-777. The Indian Air Force acquired the Boeing-777 from Air India when the government divested from the firm. The IAF also acquired six A-321 aircraft from Air India, these aircraft will be converted to Airborne Early Warning and Control aircraft.

title: J-K: Pakistani JeM terrorist`s body found in Doda, M4 rifle recovered
teaser: Officials said joint security forces recovered the remains of the terrorist, who had been killed earlier during an operation in the district. The night-enabled M4 rifle was also recovered from the spot.
description: Officials said joint security forces recovered the remains of the terrorist, who had been killed earlier during an operation in the district. The night-enabled M4 rifle was also recovered from the spot.
content: The body of a Pakistani Jaish-e-Mohammad (JeM) terrorist, along with his M4 rifle, was recovered from Jammu and Kashmir’s Doda district on Saturday, police said. Officials said joint security forces recovered the remains of the terrorist, who had been killed earlier during an operation in the district. The night-enabled M4 rifle was also recovered from the spot. “You Can Run But You Can't Hide!” the J&K Police said in a post on X. The operation was jointly carried out by the J&K Police’s Special Operations Group (SOG) Doda, the Army’s Rashtriya Rifles (RR) and the Central Reserve Police Force (CRPF). The operation took place in the Seoj Dhar forest area, which connects Doda’s Bhaderwah with the neighbouring districts of Udhampur and Kathua. The recovery comes amid intensified anti-terror operations across Doda, Kishtwar and Ramban. Security forces have stepped up area domination patrols and search operations following earlier gunfights in high-altitude areas and intelligence inputs about militant movement in the upper reaches. Combing operations have also been intensified in the dense forests and difficult mountain terrain of Doda as security forces continue efforts to track down remaining militant networks. Across the Jammu division, security forces have increased their presence in rugged, high-altitude forest areas and mountain passes, where foreign militants are believed to have shifted towards operating from remote terrain. The Army has deployed more than 4,000 specialised personnel, including Para Commandos and mountain warfare troops, across the hilly districts as part of efforts to counter the shift from urban areas to jungle warfare. Several major operations have been carried out in the region in recent months. In Rajouri, Operation Sheruwali was a multi-week joint operation involving the Indian Army, J&K Police and the CRPF in the densely forested areas of Gambhir Mughlan and Dorimal in the Manjakote sector. Security forces carried out fire assaults on suspected cave hideouts where heavily armed militants were believed to be hiding. In Poonch’s Surankote and Mendhar forests, security forces have regularly conducted Cordon and Search Operations (CASOs) in areas including Bhata Dhurian, Nar and Surankote. The operations followed intelligence inputs tracking suspicious movement from lower Pangai and nearby frontier villages. In Kathua and Samba, security forces have also conducted intensive operations in areas including the Ding Amb and Sanyal forests. The multi-layered searches covered several kilometres of difficult border terrain and were supported by helicopters, UAVs and sniffer dogs. During these operations, security forces uncovered well-stocked hideouts containing grenades and other equipment believed to be linked to JeM groups. title: ‘Can we have a picture?’ BRICS delegates gather around PM Modi for photo op | WATCH
teaser: A light-hearted moment took place at the BRICS summit venue when some participants approached Prime Minister Modi with a request for a group photograph.
description: A light-hearted moment took place at the BRICS summit venue when some participants approached Prime Minister Modi with a request for a group photograph.
content: Prime Minister Narendra Modi had a candid moment at the BRICS Business Forum in New Delhi on Friday when a group of participants asked for a photo. The PM obliged, sparking a lighthearted interaction at the high-profile global event. In a video of the interaction, it could be seen that a delegate asked PM Modi for a picture. Follow live updates from the BRICS summit here. "Can we have a picture?" one of the delegates was heard asking as PM Modi was about to leave the BRICS Summit venue. The Prime Minister agreed to pose for a picture with the delegates. "You are so lucky, all the ladies," said the official who took the picture of the participants with PM Modi. The comment prompted instant laughter among the assembled participants, with one of them saying, “We are all so lucky.” Prime Minister Modi walked alongside heads of state, including Russian President Vladimir Putin, Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian and South African President Cyril Ramaphosa, at the BRICS Business Forum 2026 in New Delhi on Friday. PM Modi was seen holding hands with the leaders as they walked together. Also Read | BRICS power parade: Modi, Pezeshkian, Putin, Ramaphosa strike a stunning frame PM Modi on Saturday welcomed several world leaders, including Russian President Putin and Chinese President Xi Jinping, to India for a two-day BRICS summit. The theme of India's BRICS presidency is "Building for Resilience, Innovation, Cooperation and Sustainability". Also Read | Xi Jinping's car arrives in Delhi under black covers. What we know about the 'secret' Hongqi N701 The other leaders attending the summit in New Delhi are Iranian President Pezeshkian, South African President Ramaphosa, Malaysian Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim, Indonesian President Prabowo Subianto, Abu Dhabi Crown Prince Mohamed bin Zayed Al Nahyan, Ethiopian Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed Ali, Egyptian President Abdel Fattah El-Sisi and Vietnamese Prime Minister Le Minh Hung, according to news agency PTI. UN Secretary-General Antonio Guterres, WTO Director-General Ngozi Okonjo-Iweala, WHO Chief Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus, New Development Bank (NDB) President Dilma Rousseff and Asian Infrastructure Investment Bank Chief Zou Jiayi are also attending the key summit. Also Read | Xi Jinping in India with 2 key men: Who are Cai Qi and Wang Yi? Declaring the BRICS Summit 2026 open, Prime Minister Modi said India’s chairship is based on a “people-centric and humanity-first approach.” “Greetings to you all. It gives me immense pleasure to welcome and greet all of you to India. India’s BRICS chairship is based on a people-centric and humanity-first approach. Resilience, innovation, cooperation, and sustainability have been our priorities. With these priorities, we have placed special emphasis on connecting the BRICS chairship with the common people,” he said. "With this vision, more than 350 meetings were organised, and we had the opportunity to welcome your teams in nearly 30 cities. I express my heartfelt gratitude to all of you for your active contribution and support in making India’s BRICS chairship a success," the PM added. Taking place amid global conflicts, the summit comes at a crucial time of heightened international concern.
