Progress will still seem fast, and we must make wise use of the time we gain,” Amodei wrote in an essay published on his personal website on Saturday.Amodei said AI could bring major benefits but also carried serious risks because of the power of the technology.“AI brings risks, and because it is such a powerful technology, these risks are serious,” he wrote.His call has received support from OpenAI CEO Sam Altman and Tesla chief Elon Musk. Altman said the need to pace the development of frontier AI had been a key topic of discussions at OpenAI in recent weeks.“I agree with Dario that we need to pace the frontier,” Altman said in a post on X. “Committing to having independent evaluators with employee-like access is a great idea, and we will do the same.”Musk also endorsed Amodei’s proposal, writing: “Dario is right.”Why Amodei wants AI development slowedAmodei said his concern had grown as AI development accelerated, particularly because AI systems were increasingly being used to help build the next generation of AI.“My first concern is that, since roughly this summer, AI has been advancing drastically faster, driven primarily by AI’s growing ability to build the next generation of AI,” he wrote.He referred to this process as “recursive self-improvement” and said it was beginning to happen across the industry, including at Anthropic.“Left unchecked, it could outrun our ability to understand and control these systems, and so must be pursued very carefully, if at all,” Amodei wrote.He also pointed to risks including the possibility of losing control of AI systems, misuse of AI for cyberattacks and bioterrorism, and serious economic disruption.Amodei said commercial incentives could make these risks more acute if companies engaged in a race to develop increasingly capable systems without sufficient safeguards.Anthropic proposes third-party AI evaluatorsAmodei said Anthropic would take steps to allow independent scrutiny of its AI systems.“We’ll provide third-party evaluators with permanent, employee-level access to our systems, so that they can verify adherence to our safety measures, report on incidents, and assess models’ alignment during training,” he wrote.His wider three-part plan calls for each frontier AI company to give ongoing, employee-like access to embedded third-party evaluators.He also proposed coordination among AI companies to establish common safety standards and limits on the rate of unchecked AI progress, along with global coordination on AI development.Amodei said democratic governments should coordinate with authoritarian governments while recognising the difficulties involved in verifying compliance.OpenAI testing raises safety concernsThe discussion comes amid concerns over the behaviour of increasingly capable AI systems.OpenAI had revealed during testing that some AI models broke out of their confined environment, connected to the internet and infiltrated Hugging Face, a platform used by developers to store and share code.Amodei also referred to an incident involving an OpenAI-Hugging Face system in which a swarm of AI agents staged cybersecurity attacks on targets they had not been instructed to attack.He warned that such a swarm could potentially become capable of taking over the internet.Researcher quits AI industry over concernsAmodei's comments came days after AI researcher Jacob Coxon announced that he was leaving the industry after spending three years pretraining AI models, first at OpenAI and later at Anthropic.Coxon had considered Anthropic more cautious in its approach but said both companies were moving too quickly towards increasingly autonomous systems.“Neither company is acting responsibly. They are racing straight to self-improving superintelligence and gambling with our lives,” Coxon said on Tuesday.“The people building AI earnestly believe that it could kill us all by the end of the decade,” he said in a post on X.Pretraining is the stage in which AI models absorb vast quantities of data.Superintelligence refers to the theoretical point at which AI capabilities exceed human intelligence.Amodei says AI benefits remain the goalDespite his call for slower development, Amodei said he continued to believe AI could significantly improve human life.“I have worked on AI for the last twelve years because I believe it could dramatically raise the quality of human life,” he wrote.He said AI could potentially cure major diseases in the next five to 10 years, accelerate economic growth, create a world of abundance and empowerment, and contribute to a renaissance of democracy and freedom.But he argued that achieving those benefits would require greater care over how the technology is developed.“The benefits will only be achieved if we build the technology in the right way,” Amodei wrote.He said the time gained by slowing development could be used to advance research into AI interpretability, improve operational security and strengthen safeguards at frontier AI companies.Amodei's latest call echoes an earlier appeal by Anthropic in June to slow or suspend AI development. In late July, Altman had also said AI developers might need to voluntarily slow their rapid advances to give society time to catch up.At around the same time, more than 1,000 employees at leading AI companies, including Amodei, signed a petition calling on the US government to help “deliberately pace the frontier of automated AI development”.Get the latest technology news and updates. title: ‘Those who keep changing names…’: Akhilesh, CJP, Cong target Yogi over ‘walking away’ from press conference
teaser: CJP and SP posted videos of the alleged incident and claimed that the UP chief minister walked away while a reporter continued to ask him questions.
description: CJP and SP posted videos of the alleged incident and claimed that the UP chief minister walked away while a reporter continued to ask him questions.
content: The Cockroach Janta Party (CJP), Samajwadi Party (SP) chief Akhilesh Yadav and the Congress party on Saturday targeted Uttar Pradesh chief minister Yogi Adityanath, alleging that he refused to take questions from a journalist at a press conference. CJP and Yadav both posted videos purportedly showing Adityanath walking away from the press conference after allegedly refusing to answer a journalist's questions. The BJP has not yet reacted to the criticism. CJP posted a video of the alleged incident and claimed that the UP chief minister walked away while a reporter continued to ask him questions. “This is exactly why we rank 157th out of 180 on Press Freedom Index,” it wrote. Yadav, meanwhile, said Uttar Pradesh has an “overflowing” number of questions, but the BJP-led government has “no answers”. In a Hindi post on X, the former Uttar Pradesh chief minister said a press conference should be called a "press monologue" if journalists are expected only to hear statements and are not allowed to ask questions. "Those who keep changing names should now change the name of 'press conference' to 'press monologue', because when only a statement has to be given and the press has no right to ask questions, what meaning does the word 'conference' have without dialogue?" he asked, without naming anyone. "The truth is that there is a flood of questions in Uttar Pradesh, but they have no answers," Yadav said, adding that turning away and leaving the field could also be described as running away. He alleged that the BJP-led government follows "discrimination" in governance and promotes "one-sided rhetoric" during press conferences. "What next, will they also say that they are not in the mood to listen to questions?" he asked. The Congress claimed that the woman journalist was removed from her job after she tried to ask a question at Adityanath's press conference. The party alleged that she was surrounded and threatened at the BJP office, with the threats reportedly including bulldozer action. Uttar Pradesh Congress chief Ajay Rai, in a statement, said denying a journalist employment and security for asking questions reflects the "dictatorial" nature of a government that claims to provide good governance. Rai said the alleged incident was not only an attack on the journalist but also a direct assault on the fourth pillar of democracy. He said the Congress stands with journalists and will oppose such actions. teaser: Dipke visited Adori, Korka and Bondari villages to meet the families of tribal children who allegedly died due to infectious diseases.
description: Dipke visited Adori, Korka and Bondari villages to meet the families of tribal children who allegedly died due to infectious diseases.
content: Cockroach Janta Party founder Abhijeet Dipke was allegedly heckled by a group of people who appeared to be social media influencers or content creators during his visit to Madhya Pradesh's Balaghat district on Saturday. Dipke visited Adori, Korka and Bondari villages to meet the families of tribal children who allegedly died due to infectious diseases and to gather information about local healthcare facilities, news agency PTI reported. A viral video showed a woman 'influencer' sticking a mic in Dipke's face as he was driving away in a car, and asking him if he had come there to "do politics on corpses" and why he was visiting the area so late. Dipke was heard saying he apologised for visiting the area late. The woman was also heard saying, "A good road has been constructed here. Can't you see it?" As the situation escalated, CJP workers accompanying Dipke put him in another car and took him away. As he left, the woman was heard saying "he ran away, he ran away." Local journalists said they were surprised to see this group of social media influencers from outside turning up in the remote village, and wondered if they had been sent by someone to disrupt the CJP founder's visit. Earlier this week, the Jabalpur bench of the Madhya Pradesh High Court sought a response from the state government over the deaths of more than 30 children in the region. The division bench of Acting Chief Justice Vivek Rusia and Justice Pradeep Mittal issued notices to the state Health Department, Women and Child Development Department, Balaghat collector and others while hearing a public interest litigation. The PIL alleged that children were not receiving adequate treatment and that around 400 children were being treated at a hospital with a capacity of 50 beds. title: Mumbai Court Acquits Absconding Man In 1989 Dacoity Case After Trial In Absentia Under BNSS
teaser: Mumbai, September 12, 2026: The special court on Thursday acquitted an absconding man booked in 1989 for dacoity after conducting his trial under the provisions for trial in absentia. The same judge has so far closed several cases after con
description: Mumbai, September 12, 2026: The special court on Thursday acquitted an absconding man booked in 1989 for dacoity after conducting his trial under the provisions for trial in absentia. The same judge has so far closed several cases after con
content: Mumbai, September 12, 2026: The special court on Thursday acquitted an absconding man booked in 1989 for dacoity after conducting his trial under the provisions for trial in absentia. The same judge has so far closed several cases after conducting trial even when the accused are still wanted. The same judge is now going to hear the prosecution's plea to conduct the trial against absconding accused in the 26/11 terror attack case in their absence. Cases From Past Decades Reopened Special judge Satyanarayan Navander has so far disposed of several cases registered in the 90s and 80s and pending before the court as the accused were absconding. In what is said to be the first of the cases he had, in December last year, acquitted Rajendra Giri, resident of Sakinaka, for having looted a house with valuables worth Rs 3.80 lakh at gunpoint on March 31, 1992. Similarly, in many such cases, the court appointed a lawyer to defend the absconding accused who had been declared as proclaimed offenders, from the panel of legal aid lawyers to conduct the trial in their absence. FPJ Shorts Mumbai Court Acquits Absconding Man In 1989 Dacoity Case After Trial In Absentia Under BNSS Ganeshotsav Rush Chokes Thane’s Konkan Corridor; Buses Take Hours To Reach Mumbai-Goa Highway Mumbai: NSCT Inaugurates Al Shifa Dental Clinic And Rahat Care Support Centre At Vikhroli Parksite Asian Games Clash Gives India ODI Headache, Opens Door For Rishabh Pant And Yashasvi Jaiswal Trial In Absentia Under BNSS Special judge Navander had in his judgment dated December 18, 2025, said, “as per section 356 of BNSS (deals with proceedings against proclaimed offender) when a person is declared as a proclaimed offender and it is found that, he has absconded to evade trial, and there is no immediate prospect of arresting him, he can be tried as if he is present. The provision of trial in absentia has been thus provided by BNSS, provided the accused is defended by a competent lawyer.” After Navander, now other courts have also initiated the process to conduct the trial in the cases which are pending because of the absence of the accused. Special judge A. S. Wairagade, dealing with cases of child sexual abuse, also opened around five cases last month which were registered between 1988 to 2003, where accused are still absconding. The court has now framed charges against them to conduct trial in absence of the accused. More Dormant Cases Taken Up Similarly, special judge Mahesh Jadhav, too, opened dormant cases pending because the accused are absconding. The special court on September 9 acquitted resident of Thane, Jaspalsingh Chaulansingh, booked for murder charges in August 1986. The court conducted a trial against Chaulansingh while he still remains absconding. Meanwhile, the other accused in the case were acquitted in 1996. Also Watch: Read Also Mumbai 13/7 Triple Blast Case: Special MCOCA Court Grants Bail To Accused After 15 Years As... The special judge has so far disposed of four such cases registered between 1986 to 1988 and concluded trial against absconding accused under the provisions of Section 356 of BNSS. Published - September 12, 2026 11:17 pm IST - New Delhi Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian meets with UAE Crown Prince Khaled bin Mohamed bin Zayed Al Nahyan on the sidelines of the BRICS Summit. | Photo Credit: ANI Against the backdrop of continued hostilities in West Asia, Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian and the Crown Prince of Abu Dhabi, Khaled bin Mohamed bin Zayed Al Nahyan, held talks in New Delhi on Saturday (September 12, 2026) on the sidelines of the 18th BRICS Summit. The two sides discussed the regional hostilities and expressed support for "de-escalation". The conversation came ten days after Iran targeted military installations in the United Arab Emirates (UAE). The ‘New Delhi Declaration’, adopted at the BRICS Summit and announced by Prime Minister Narendra Modi, has expressed “deep concern” about the multiple conflicts in West Asia, but stopped short of naming any of the major stakeholders, including the United States, in the text. title: 5,036 feral pigs removed from Santa Cruz Island; fox population rebounded
teaser: Feral pigs were eradicated from Santa Cruz Island, facilitating a resurgence in fox populations. With bald eagles no longer in the area, golden eagles preyed on the island's foxes. In response, conservationists captured the golden eagles an
description: Feral pigs were eradicated from Santa Cruz Island, facilitating a resurgence in fox populations. With bald eagles no longer in the area, golden eagles preyed on the island's foxes. In response, conservationists captured the golden eagles an
content: An ambitious conservation project off the coast of California has helped save the endangered Santa Cruz Island fox from near extinction. The rescue effort involved removing 5,036 feral pigs, allowing the native island fox (Urocyon littoralis santacruzae) population to recover from fewer than 100 animals to more than 1,300 across the 96-square-mile island. According to historical records and ecological recovery reports from the National Park Service and The Nature Conservancy, the crisis began after domestic pigs brought to Santa Cruz Island in the 1850s escaped and formed a large wild population.Unintended food source brought a new predatorFor decades, the feral pig population grew rapidly across Santa Cruz Island. The pigs damaged native vegetation and produced a steady supply of piglets throughout the year. This large food supply attracted golden eagles (Aquila chrysaetos) from mainland California. Golden eagles had previously avoided the northern Channel Islands because native bald eagles (Haliaeetus leucocephalus) defended their territories and kept rival birds of prey away. However, pesticide pollution in the mid-20th century wiped out bald eagles across the region. With bald eagles gone and thousands of piglets available as prey, golden eagles began breeding on Santa Cruz Island in the late 1990s. The golden eagles first arrived to hunt young pigs, but they soon began attacking the smaller and less wary island foxes. Because the foxes had evolved without regular aerial predators, they were active during the day and had little experience hiding from attacks from above. By 2000, heavy predation by golden eagles had reduced the Santa Cruz Island fox population by 95 per cent, leaving the subspecies close to extinction.Multi-stage campaign restores the island ecosystemTo stop the decline, the National Park Service joined The Nature Conservancy in a major recovery project on Santa Cruz Island. Wildlife biologists concluded that protecting the foxes meant removing the non-native pigs that supported the golden eagle population. Conservation teams divided the rugged island into management zones and built miles of internal fencing to stop pigs from escaping into thick vegetation. Between 2005 and 2006, specialist teams removed all 5,036 feral pigs from the island. The operation used ground tracking, aerial support and trained hunting dogs. At the same time, biologists captured golden eagles and moved them to remote mountain areas on the California mainland. To prevent the birds from returning, conservationists also reintroduced bald eagles to their former nesting areas across the Channel Islands.Captive breeding helps fox population recoverAs the pig eradication programme continued, wildlife specialists set up a captive breeding facility on Santa Cruz Island to protect the remaining foxes from golden eagle attacks. Biologists captured some of the last wild foxes and paired them in protected breeding enclosures while maintaining genetic diversity. As golden eagles were removed and bald eagles returned to the region, researchers began releasing captive-born foxes into the wild. The recovery was rapid. National Park Service surveys showed wild fox numbers increasing as native vegetation began recovering from years of damage caused by feral pigs. By the time federal authorities removed the Santa Cruz Island fox from the Endangered Species List, its population had recovered to more than 1,300 breeding animals. The Santa Cruz Island project became one of the fastest wildlife recoveries under the US Endangered Species Act. It showed how removing invasive mammals can help restore native wildlife and ecosystems on islands.

The Hindu On Books Books of the week, reviews, excerpts, new titles and features. Published - September 12, 2026 11:12 pm IST - ERODE Revenue Minister K.A. Sengottaiyan. | Photo Credit: M. GOVARTHAN Minister for Revenue and Disaster Management K.A. Sengottaiyan said on Saturday that the Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam would achieve a huge victory in the byelections for Maduranthakam and Dharapuram constituencies and those to other constituencies, which would be announced by the Election Commission of India (EC) after the High Court delivered its verdict on September 28. He was speaking to reporters after attending the centenary celebrations of the Kaliappampalayam Panchayat Union Primary School near Gobichettipalayam. He distributed prizes to students who had won various competitions. Asked about development works for schools that had completed 100 years, Mr. Sengottaiyan said all parts of the State were being monitored directly by Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay through the School Education Department and all schemes would be implemented effectively. On the delay in disbursal of social security assistance, he said financial assistance due from the Centre to senior citizens, deserted women, widows, and persons with disabilities had not been released to around 27,412 beneficiaries. The State government had recommended that the Centre release the funds by September 14, he said, adding that the government had taken steps to ensure that the beneficiaries received the assistance on Monday. On the byelection, Mr. Sengottaiyan said: “Wherever we go, we emerge victorious. The court verdict for the election petitions in the other constituencies is expected on September 28. Once the High Court delivers its verdict, the EC will announce the date for the byelections.” Copyright© 2026, THG PUBLISHING PVT LTD. or its affiliated companies. All rights reserved. The Hindu On Books Books of the week, reviews, excerpts, new titles and features. Former Union Minister A. Raja and DMK south district secretary Ma. Subramanian, along with other party leaders, at the demonstration held at Saidapet in Chennai on Saturday. | Photo Credit: Special arrangement The DMK on Saturday staged demonstrations across Tamil Nadu, condemning the remarks made by Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay in the Assembly against former Chief Minister M.K. Stalin. Speaking on Monday during the debate on the Demand for Grants for the Police Department, Mr. Vijay made certain remarks regarding Mr. Stalin’s arrest under the MISA. Condemning his remarks, the DMK staged protests in district headquarters across Tamil Nadu on Saturday. In Chennai, the demonstration was held in two locations. While former Union Minister A. Raja addressed the gathering at a protest led by the party’s south district secretary Ma. Subramanian in Saidapet, another protest was held near the Collectorate, led by the party’s organising secretary R.S. Bharathi, with Chennai Mayor R. Priya and others participating. Speaking at the Saidapet demonstration, Mr. Raja sharply condemned Mr. Vijay for his remarks. Certain remarks made by Mr. Raja regarding a Minister during this speech have also drawn criticism on social media. Tamil Nadu Congress Committee president B. Manickam Tagore has condemned Mr. Raja’s remarks. In Tiruchi, the protest was held in front of the Marakkadai M.G.R. statue. Former Minister and DMK principal secretary K.N. Nehru presided over and addressed the protest, which was attended by former Minister Anbil Mahesh and MP Salma, among others. Similarly, in Salem, Rajya Sabha member Tiruchi Siva delivered a special address at a protest held on the Salem Fort premises, presided over by former Minister Rajendran. Slogans were raised during the demonstrations demanding, among other things, the expunction of the remarks made against the DMK president from the Assembly records. The Erode North and South district units of the DMK staged a demonstration near the Kalaimadu Silai area, led by Erode North district secretary N. Nallasivam and former Minister and Erode South district secretary S. Muthusamy. Addressing the demonstration held outside the Karur Head Post Office, former Minister V. Senthilbalaji said: “Chief Minister Vijay and TVK functionaries must stop speaking slanderously about DMK leaders.” Copyright© 2026, THG PUBLISHING PVT LTD. or its affiliated companies. description: New Delhi, September 12, 2026: Chinese President Xi Jinping said on Saturday that China and India are partners, not rivals, and opportunities, not threats, for each other's development during his meeting with Prime Minister Narendra Modi on
content: New Delhi, September 12, 2026: Chinese President Xi Jinping said on Saturday that China and India are partners, not rivals, and opportunities, not threats, for each other's development during his meeting with Prime Minister Narendra Modi on the sidelines of the 18th BRICS Summit in New Delhi, the Chinese Ministry of Foreign Affairs said in a statement. China-India Ties See Further Enhancement "In the past two years, he (President Xi Jinping) and Prime Minister Modi have met twice, guiding China-India relations from a 'restart' to a 'further enhancement'. Institutional exchanges between the two countries have gradually resumed, the cooperation list has been continuously extended, and bilateral trade has reached a new high," the Ministry added. It said that China and India have different national conditions and can fully learn from each other's strengths, support each other, achieve mutual success, and develop together. Both sides should keep the future of humanity in mind and prioritise the well-being of their people, working together to promote high-quality development of BRICS cooperation and provide more positive energy for promoting world peace, stability, development, and prosperity," the Ministry stressed. Xi Shares Four-Point Approach It noted that President Xi shared four points on promoting the steady and long-term development of China-India relations. "First, we should calibrate our direction with an objective and rational strategic understanding. China and India are partners, not rivals, and opportunities, not threats, for each other's development. This strategic judgment is based on the development stages of both countries and the international environment, and it aligns with the common interests of both countries and their people," the statement said. "Second, we should achieve mutual success through win-win cooperation," it added. The Ministry said that both sides should focus on development as the greatest common denominator, strengthening friendly exchanges and mutually beneficial cooperation. Focus On Border Peace "Third, we should eliminate interference with the political wisdom of mutual respect and understanding. We should commit to the parallel development and mutual promotion of bilateral relations and border issues, maintaining peace and tranquillity in border areas," the Ministry noted. "Fourth, we should benefit the world through open and inclusive multilateral cooperation," the Ministry said. title: AI Says: Why Is Modak Lord Ganesha’s Favourite Sweet?
teaser: Legend of Anasuya's FeastAccording to Hindu mythology, Lord Shiva, Goddess Parvati, and young Ganesha visited the hermitage of Sage Atri and his wife, Anasuya. Anasuya served feast after feast, but Ganesha's immense appetite remained unappe
description: Legend of Anasuya's FeastAccording to Hindu mythology, Lord Shiva, Goddess Parvati, and young Ganesha visited the hermitage of Sage Atri and his wife, Anasuya. Anasuya served feast after feast, but Ganesha's immense appetite remained unappe
content: Legend of Anasuya's Feast According to Hindu mythology, Lord Shiva, Goddess Parvati, and young Ganesha visited the hermitage of Sage Atri and his wife, Anasuya. Anasuya served feast after feast, but Ganesha's immense appetite remained unappeased. Finally, she served a small, sweet dumpling—the modak. Upon eating a single modak, Ganesha burped with satisfaction, signaling he was completely full, which in turn satiated Lord Shiva as well. Symbol of Divine Knowledge Etymologically, "Moda" means joy, bliss, or happiness, while "Ka" means a small part or piece. Spiritually, the modak represents spiritual wisdom (Gyana). Its pointed top symbolizes the focused pursuit of higher knowledge, while the outer shell hides the sweet inner filling (coconut and jaggery), representing the hidden bliss of self-realization. title: Is Comfort The New Luxury? 7 Things Modern Travellers Expect From Hospitality Brands
teaser: Luxury in hospitality no longer means opulent lobbies, lavish interiors, or a long list of facilities. These things still matter, but they're no longer what guests notice first. What travellers pay attention to today is whether a stay feels
description: Luxury in hospitality no longer means opulent lobbies, lavish interiors, or a long list of facilities. These things still matter, but they're no longer what guests notice first. What travellers pay attention to today is whether a stay feels
content: Luxury in hospitality no longer means opulent lobbies, lavish interiors, or a long list of facilities. These things still matter, but they're no longer what guests notice first. What travellers pay attention to today is whether a stay feels effortless — whether the property understands them, adjusts to them, and lets them get on with their day without friction. This holds regardless of why someone is travelling. A guest on a business trip, someone relocating for work, a professional working remotely from a new city, or a family on holiday — all of them, in their own way, want the property to fit around their life rather than the other way round. As travel patterns keep changing, hospitality brands are having to relearn what actually makes a stay memorable, and increasingly, the answer is comfort rather than extravagance. Here are seven things modern travellers have come to expect from hospitality brands. Recognition, not just accommodation FPJ Shorts Ganeshotsav 2026: Ganesha Idol Topples During Rain In Nallasopara; 4-5 Devotees Escape Unhurt | VIDEO BRICS Summit 2026: Chinese President Xi Jinping Skips PM Modi’s Gala Dinner In Delhi BRICS Summit 2026: ‘China And India Are Partners, Not Rivals,’ Says President Xi Jinping In Meeting With PM Modi | VIDEO BRICS Summit 2026: World Leaders Arrive In Delhi For Gala Dinner Hosted By PM Modi At Bharat Mandapam | VIDEO Guests notice when a property remembers them — a preferred floor, a dietary note from a previous visit, a small habit picked up without being asked twice. This isn't about grand gestures. It's the difference between being treated as a booking reference and being treated as a returning guest. Properties that get this right tend to build loyalty that has nothing to do with loyalty programmes. Technology that helps Digital check-in, app-based requests, and quick online bookings have become standard, and guests expect them to work without friction. But technology is at its best when it removes the small annoyances — not when it replaces the person who can actually solve a problem on the spot. The properties that guests remember fondly are usually the ones where a fast digital process is backed by a team that steps in the moment something needs a human decision. Same standard, every time One excellent stay followed by an inconsistent one does more damage to a brand than a mediocre stay ever could. Guests today expect the same level of cleanliness, service, and reliability whether they're checking in on a Tuesday afternoon or a Saturday night, at a flagship city property or a smaller one in a Tier-2 market. Consistency across every touchpoint — not just the obvious ones — has become a basic expectation rather than a bonus. Genuine sense of place Travellers increasingly want their stay to say something about where they actually are. That could mean a breakfast menu that reflects the region, honest recommendations for a neighbourhood café instead of a generic tourist list, or simply staff who know the city well enough to give useful advice. A hotel that feels identical in every city misses an opportunity guests are actively looking for. Sustainability that's practised Guests have become fairly good at telling the difference between a property that has genuinely rethought its water and energy use, sourcing, and waste management, and one that has simply added the word "eco-friendly" to its marketing. The brands that earn trust here are the ones where sustainability shows up in daily operations — not just in a printed card left on the pillow. Wellness built into the stay Rest has become part of the reason people travel, not just something that happens between activities. Comfortable, well-lit rooms, food that doesn't feel like an afterthought, and spaces that allow a guest to actually slow down have become meaningful differentiators. This matters even more for longer stays, where a guest is essentially living their daily life out of that room for weeks at a time. Value measured in experience Price still matters, but it's rarely the deciding factor anymore. Guests weigh it against everything else — how smooth the stay was, how much they didn't have to worry about, whether the service felt attentive rather than transactional. A well-priced stay that leaves a guest frustrated loses out to a slightly costlier one that leaves them satisfied. Value, in the end, is judged by what a guest walks away feeling, not just what they paid. Common thread None of these expectations are really about luxury in the traditional sense. They're about a property understanding who its guests are and adjusting to them, rather than expecting guests to adjust to the property. As travel patterns keep evolving — longer stays, more frequent relocations, blurred lines between work and leisure — the hospitality brands that stay relevant will be the ones built around this understanding from the ground up. Guests may not remember the exact finish of a countertop a year from now. They will remember whether a stay felt effortless, whether they were looked after, and whether the place understood what they actually needed. That, increasingly, is what guests mean when they talk about a great stay. (Jaideep Ahuja, Managing Director & CEO, Ahuja Residences)

Consistency across every touchpoint — not just the obvious ones — has become a basic expectation rather than a bonus. Genuine sense of place Travellers increasingly want their stay to say something about where they actually are. That could mean a breakfast menu that reflects the region, honest recommendations for a neighbourhood café instead of a generic tourist list, or simply staff who know the city well enough to give useful advice. A hotel that feels identical in every city misses an opportunity guests are actively looking for. Sustainability that's practised Guests have become fairly good at telling the difference between a property that has genuinely rethought its water and energy use, sourcing, and waste management, and one that has simply added the word "eco-friendly" to its marketing. The brands that earn trust here are the ones where sustainability shows up in daily operations — not just in a printed card left on the pillow. Wellness built into the stay Rest has become part of the reason people travel, not just something that happens between activities. Comfortable, well-lit rooms, food that doesn't feel like an afterthought, and spaces that allow a guest to actually slow down have become meaningful differentiators. This matters even more for longer stays, where a guest is essentially living their daily life out of that room for weeks at a time. Guests weigh it against everything else — how smooth the stay was, how much they didn't have to worry about, whether the service felt attentive rather than transactional. A well-priced stay that leaves a guest frustrated loses out to a slightly costlier one that leaves them satisfied. title: To Stop Irregularities In DE, Departments Asked Opt For Online Portal
teaser: Bhopal (Madhya Pradesh): The state government has asked all departments to conduct enquiries through the online portal to check irregularities in investigations.The government made it clear that the departments should opt for the portal by
description: Bhopal (Madhya Pradesh): The state government has asked all departments to conduct enquiries through the online portal to check irregularities in investigations.The government made it clear that the departments should opt for the portal by
content: Bhopal (Madhya Pradesh): The state government has asked all departments to conduct enquiries through the online portal to check irregularities in investigations. The government made it clear that the departments should opt for the portal by September 30. An order issued by the General Administration Department (GAD) directed all wings to use the DE portal for enquiries and the e-HRMS portal for other work related to employees. The departments often keep files suppressed for a long time because of manual inquiry. The government has prepared the DE portal to stop this malpractice, but since many departments have avoided it, the administration has become strict. GAD has directed the departments to use the online portal to process any paper -- from appointment to retirement of an employee. The online system should be used to maintain leave records, travels and other services, including promotion and transfers, GAD said. Information about employees will be available in a digital profile, which also remains compulsory. title: Decomposed body of ‘Pak Jaish terrorist’, M4 rifle found in J&K's Doda
teaser: Authorities in Doda's Divshetar have discovered the decomposed body of a suspected Jaish-e-Mohammed terrorist from Pakistan. The remains, thought to have been buried in snow for some time after a previous operation, were found with an M4 ri
description: Authorities in Doda's Divshetar have discovered the decomposed body of a suspected Jaish-e-Mohammed terrorist from Pakistan. The remains, thought to have been buried in snow for some time after a previous operation, were found with an M4 ri
content: JAMMU: Decomposed remains of a suspected Pakistani Jaish-e-Mohammed (JeM) terrorist was found Saturday along with an M4 rifle in Divshetar area of J&K’s Doda district, with security forces suggesting the corpse had been lying in the snow-capped hills since the man’s death in a past operation.Some locals noticed the body in Seoj Dhar zone and intimated authorities. “Security forces are conducting further investigations to ascertain the identity of the deceased and other details,” an official said.A J&K Police post on X, apparently aimed at terrorists, pointed towards an encounter death. “You Can Run But You Can’t Hide. SOG Doda, Rashtriya Rifles (RR) and CRPF retrieved the remains of a Pakistani Jaish-e-Mohammed terrorist who had been neutralised earlier in a joint operation. A night vision-enabled M4 rifle was also recovered,” the post read.Searches to smoke out terrorists from the higher reaches of Doda, Kishtwar, Kathua, Udhampur, Rajouri and Poonch districts in Jammu zone have been common over the past two years, resulting in nearly a dozen encounters.Barely a month ago, four suspected terrorists were spotted scaling the Ramtund peak in Doda’s Seoj Dhar area, triggering intensive searches.In Feb this year, Doda cops pasted posters seeking information about Saifullah, a self-styled Jaish commander from Pakistan suspected to be holed up in the Chatroo belt of adjoining Kishtwar district.In Sept last year, an Army jawan died from injuries suffered in an encounter after terrorists opened fire on a patrolling team in the forests of Doda’s Bhaderwah.Get the latest India News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

title: Fire at nursing home in Chile kills 16 residents
teaser: Ten people were evacuated from the home in Araucanía region in central Chile.
description: Ten people were evacuated from the home in Araucanía region in central Chile.
content: Fire at nursing home in Chile kills 16 residents 9 minutes ago Share Save Add as preferred on Google Getty Images At least 16 elderly residents have died in a fire at a nursing home in Chile, according to authorities. Ten others were evacuated after a blaze broke out at El Edén home in Pitrufquén, around 640km (400 miles) south of the capital Santiago, on Friday evening. Jorge Granada, a prosecutor leading the case, said it was not clear at this stage what caused the incident. Chile's President José Antonio Kast said he had ordered a review into the condition of nursing homes across the country. "We will fully collaborate with the justice system to clarify what happened, determine where failures may have existed in oversight or prevention, identify what alerts were raised and what actions were taken in response to them," Kast said. "We need to know the truth and, based on that, correct whatever is necessary to do everything possible to prevent a tragedy like this from happening again," thre president added. The fire, which began at around 22:30 (01:30 GMT) was finally put out on Saturday morning. On Saturday, firefighters were still clearing debris and removing collapsed corrugated metal roofing. Police cordoned off the area for safety. "It is a situation that fills our souls with great sorrow and pain. We have been... providing support to the families," said local mayor Jacqueline Romero. Chile Care homes

title: Man hid inside giant Roman storage jar 1,600 years ago and never came out
teaser: In a remarkable excavation at Deultum, Bulgaria, archaeologists uncovered the remains of a young man entombed within a sizable storage jar. The evidence indicates he sought refuge there during a devastating attack, likely after the flames h
description: In a remarkable excavation at Deultum, Bulgaria, archaeologists uncovered the remains of a young man entombed within a sizable storage jar. The evidence indicates he sought refuge there during a devastating attack, likely after the flames h
content: More than 1,600 years ago, as fire engulfed a Roman settlement in what is now Bulgaria, a young man appears to have made a desperate decision: he climbed inside a huge storage jar and hid. He never came out. Archaeologists uncovered his remains inside the vessel during excavations at the ancient Roman colony of Deultum in southeastern Bulgaria. The discovery, first reported by Live Science and subsequently detailed by Archaeology Magazine, offers a rare glimpse into the chaos of an ancient attack.A skeleton hidden inside a Roman storage jarThe remains were discovered on August 10 inside a Late Roman turret forming part of Deultum’s western gate. The individual was found at the bottom of a large ceramic vessel known as a dolium, which Romans used to store commodities including wine and olive oil.The surviving portion of the vessel measures roughly 1 metre across. Some ancient dolia were enormous, capable of holding more than 1,000 litres. Finding human remains inside the city was unexpected. Archaeologists believe the inhabitants later levelled the damaged remains of the tower and constructed a new, higher floor over the ruins. But the jar has preserved something remarkably intimate: the final moments of someone who, faced with a burning Roman settlement, apparently believed that the safest place left was inside a giant storage vessel.

title: Dog Comes From Lanka To Indore For Cataract Care
teaser: Indore (Madhya Pradesh): A nine-year-old female Yorkshire Terrier named Annie has arrived in Indore from Sri Lanka for cataract surgery, reflecting an emerging trend of medical tourism for pets alongside humans.Annie has been suffering from
description: Indore (Madhya Pradesh): A nine-year-old female Yorkshire Terrier named Annie has arrived in Indore from Sri Lanka for cataract surgery, reflecting an emerging trend of medical tourism for pets alongside humans.Annie has been suffering from
content: Indore (Madhya Pradesh): A nine-year-old female Yorkshire Terrier named Annie has arrived in Indore from Sri Lanka for cataract surgery, reflecting an emerging trend of medical tourism for pets alongside humans. Annie has been suffering from cataracts, which caused whitening of the eye lenses and reduced her vision. Since specialised veterinary ophthalmologists for cataract surgery are limited in Sri Lanka, her owner, US citizen Bethany Ann Hopkins, who currently lives there, decided to bring Annie to India for treatment. Veterinary surgeon and eye surgery specialist Dr Narendra Chauhan said his centre has been performing manual cataract surgeries since 2014 and sutureless phaco surgery since 2016. He said only a few centres in India offer specialised eye surgeries for pets, while veterinarians from abroad are also trained at the centre. Treatment cost was another factor behind the decision. According to Dr Chauhan, a cataract surgery costing around Rs 1 lakh in India can cost up to Rs 6 lakh in the US, while the technology and equipment used are comparable to American and European clinics. India also offers shorter travel time from Sri Lanka. title: Lost Phone Costs 73-Year-Old Elderly Labourer His Savings In Indore
teaser: Indore (Madhya Pradesh): A 73-year-old labourer fell victim to online fraud after an unidentified person activated a UPI app on his lost mobile phone and siphoned Rs 3.34 lakh from his bank account over five days under the Sanwer police sta
description: Indore (Madhya Pradesh): A 73-year-old labourer fell victim to online fraud after an unidentified person activated a UPI app on his lost mobile phone and siphoned Rs 3.34 lakh from his bank account over five days under the Sanwer police sta
content: Indore (Madhya Pradesh): A 73-year-old labourer fell victim to online fraud after an unidentified person activated a UPI app on his lost mobile phone and siphoned Rs 3.34 lakh from his bank account over five days under the Sanwer police station's jurisdiction. The victim, Madanlal Chauhan, a resident of Ganesh Colony in Dharampuri, reported that the incident occurred after he lost his phone at the Dharampuri weekly market on March 16. Despite extensive searching, he could not trace the device. He subsequently obtained a replacement SIM card for his registered number. title: Food Inspections Expose Kitchen Hygiene Lapses At 5 Top City Hotels
teaser: Indore (Madhya Pradesh): The Food Safety Administration conducted surprise inspections at five major hotels and found irregularities there on Saturday. Senior food safety officer Manish Swami informed Free Press that the inspections covered
description: Indore (Madhya Pradesh): The Food Safety Administration conducted surprise inspections at five major hotels and found irregularities there on Saturday. Senior food safety officer Manish Swami informed Free Press that the inspections covered
content: Indore (Madhya Pradesh): The Food Safety Administration conducted surprise inspections at five major hotels and found irregularities there on Saturday. Senior food safety officer Manish Swami informed Free Press that the inspections covered Hotel Marriott, Hotel The Park, Radisson Blu, Radisson RED and Hotel Grand Sheraton. Officials checked food storage, labelling, kitchen hygiene, medical fitness records of food handlers, FIFO/FEFO practices, drinking water testing and other safety standards. At Hotel Marriott, operated by Shri Balaji Landmark Hotel Pvt Ltd, samples of paneer, peanut and sugar powder were collected. Officials found waterlogging and slippery conditions in and around the kitchen, lack of proper anti-slip rubber mats, old and unhygienic chopping boards, faulty dustbins and rusting storage trays. Shortcomings were also found in the pesticide testing report of drinking water, drainage and ceiling leakage. The hotel had not uploaded its audit report on the FoSCoS portal, while detachable stickers were found on some packaged food products. Officials found rusting on part of the kitchen platform, improperly cleaned cooking pots and doors without automatic closers. The temperature of the milk products storage area was not displayed outside. Detachable labels were found on some food items, bills for incoming food materials were not properly maintained and medical fitness records were incomplete. At Radisson Blu, Vijay Nagar, some imported food products lacked required importer details, including name, address and FSSAI licence or registration details. Labelling issues were found on packets of Kulcha Bread and Shahi Jeera. The store was not properly organised for effective FIFO/FEFO practices, while medical fitness records were not available in the prescribed format. At Radisson RED, Scheme No. 54, officials found labelling deficiencies and improper storage organisation under FIFO/FEFO practices. Medical fitness certificates or records were not available in the required format. Samples of curd, cashew pieces and peanuts were collected. At Hotel Grand Sheraton, samples of paneer, sunflower seeds and raisins were collected. Some sunflower seeds found in poor condition were destroyed on the spot in the interest of public health. The hotel lacked a pesticide testing report for water. The management was directed to use non-porous chopping boards and proper anti-slip rubber mats. Detachable stickers were also found on some raw materials purchased from local vendors. The Food Safety Administration said notices are being issued to establishments where violations of food safety, hygiene, storage, labelling or other prescribed standards were found. title: Pollution Threat: NGT Seeks Response From Govt, MPPCB And BMC Illegal Plastic Factories Put Nearly 2 Lakh Residents At Risk In Bhopal
teaser: Bhopal (Madhya Pradesh): The National Green Tribunal (NGT) has taken suo motu cognisance of the serious health and environmental risks allegedly posed to nearly 2 lakh residents by around 50 illegally operating plastic factories in the city
description: Bhopal (Madhya Pradesh): The National Green Tribunal (NGT) has taken suo motu cognisance of the serious health and environmental risks allegedly posed to nearly 2 lakh residents by around 50 illegally operating plastic factories in the city
content: Bhopal (Madhya Pradesh): The National Green Tribunal (NGT) has taken suo motu cognisance of the serious health and environmental risks allegedly posed to nearly 2 lakh residents by around 50 illegally operating plastic factories in the city. It has sought detailed responses from the Madhya Pradesh government, Central Pollution Control Board (CPCB), Madhya Pradesh Pollution Control Board (MPPCB) and Bhopal Municipal Corporation (BMC). The tribunal, while hearing the suo motu matter along with a petition filed by Anil Kumar Verma, directed the concerned authorities to submit their responses within two to three weeks. The next hearing is scheduled for Oct 29. During the hearing, MPPCB, CPCB and BMC submitted their respective affidavits and responses. The NGT directed that copies be provided to all concerned parties, who have been given two weeks to file rejoinders. Other respondents who have not yet submitted their replies have been given a final three-week deadline. Kabadi Khana emerges as plastic recycling hub The Kabadi Khana area, traditionally known as a market for used parts, has allegedly become a major hub for illegal plastic recycling. More than 50 units reportedly operate in its narrow lanes, where plastic waste is processed into granules. The operations are particularly hazardous in densely populated areas, with small and major fires reportedly breaking out at least twice a week during summer. The narrow lanes also make it difficult for fire tenders to reach the affected spots. According to MPPCB findings cited in the matter, PM10 levels in the area reach 225-250, among the highest recorded in the city. Open dismantling of e-waste to recover metals is also allegedly releasing toxic gases into the atmosphere. Single-use plastic ban remains on paper Although single-use plastic has been banned since 2022, the ground situation remains different. Around 10-12 tonnes of plastic waste reportedly reaches Adampur garbage dumpsite daily, while a similar quantity is allegedly sent to Kabadi Khana through scrap dealers for recycling. The BMC has allotted around 800 plots in the area but reportedly lacks records detailing the businesses operating on each plot. Files related to nearly 70 plots are pending cancellation over non-payment of lease rent. Experts have called for industries operating without pollution clearances and other mandatory permissions to be shifted out of densely populated areas immediately. title: Uttar Pradesh polls: BL Santhosh holds feedback sessions in Lucknow, Kanpur
teaser: BJP's BL Santhosh held meetings in UP to gather feedback on party dynamics ahead of the 2027 elections, addressing recent challenges and strategies.
description: BJP's BL Santhosh held meetings in UP to gather feedback on party dynamics ahead of the 2027 elections, addressing recent challenges and strategies.
content: As the BJP steps up its organisational preparedness for the 2027 Uttar Pradesh assembly elections, the party’s national general secretary (organisation) BL Santhosh on Saturday held marathon meetings in the state capital and Kanpur to seek feedback on ground realities and shortcomings that the party faces on the road to the polls. In Lucknow, he first met four former state presidents – Bhupendra Chaudhary, Ramapati Ram Tripathi, Swatantra Dev Singh and Surya Pratap Shahi. Sources said former state presidents shared their assessment of organisational strength in different regions, the impact of recent incidents that helped the opposition build a narrative against the BJP, including the UGC equity guidelines row, GenZ protests, quota anger, the “powerless MLA” jibe and suggestions to counter it. State general secretary (organisation) Dharampal Singh, state in-charge of the party Vinod Tawde and co-incharge Jagdish Patel were also present in addition to the state media team, including the chief state spokesperson. The second meeting was with all the newly appointed state general secretaries. “The focus was on the 2027 assembly polls in both meetings. He took feedback from us on ground realities for the BJP in the aftermath of the UGC and quota protest,” said a senior BJP leader who was present at the meeting. Santhosh sought feedback on whether there was resentment against the party among the masses, especially among the youth, upper castes and students in the political scenario that unfolded over the last two months following the NEET paper leak row, the UGC protest, and the job quota issue raised by youth. The feedback sessions will continue in the coming days as Santosh tours different regions before submitting a report to the central leadership. Santhosh briefed general secretaries on making the month-long Seva Sankalp campaign from September 17 to October 17 a success to mark 25 years of PM Narendra Modi’s public life. Leaders said feedback taken on Saturday will be factored into the strategy for Rajya Sabha and MLC (teachers’ and graduates’ constituency) polls where names are being finalised, and for the 2027 roadmap. Santhosh, who had attended the core committee meeting on Friday night with Yogi, state BJP president Pankaj Chaudhary, deputy CMs Keshav Prasad Maurya and Brajesh Pathak, left for Kanpur in the evening. In Kanpur, he held discussions with all sitting MPs from the Kanpur-Bundelkhand region as well as those who had contested the 2024 Lok Sabha elections and lost their seats. MLAs and MLCs from the region also met him and shared feedback on the political and organisational situation. The consultations also included district presidents and general secretaries from districts covering the region’s 52 assembly constituencies. He briefed the leaders about the programmes the BJP plans to undertake in the coming weeks, with the focus on strengthening the organisation and ensuring that its programmes reach the booth level. Santhosh will meet booth presidents of the Govind Nagar assembly constituency on Sunday. The booth-level functionaries will be briefed on how to take the party’s programmes to the ground and will also receive training for the task.

MLAs and MLCs from the region also met him and shared feedback on the political and organisational situation. The consultations also included district presidents and general secretaries from districts covering the region’s 52 assembly constituencies. He briefed the leaders about the programmes the BJP plans to undertake in the coming weeks, with the focus on strengthening the organisation and ensuring that its programmes reach the booth level. Santhosh will meet booth presidents of the Govind Nagar assembly constituency on Sunday. The booth-level functionaries will be briefed on how to take the party’s programmes to the ground and will also receive training for the task.

title: Nitin Nabin’s whirlwind Uttar Pradesh tour to follow Santhosh-Tawde meetings for reality check ahead of 2027 polls
teaser: While his programme is yet to be formally announced, party functionaries said the national president was likely to hold meetings with state and regional leaders as well as grassroots workers to take stock of the organisation and the politic
description: While his programme is yet to be formally announced, party functionaries said the national president was likely to hold meetings with state and regional leaders as well as grassroots workers to take stock of the organisation and the politic
content: Bharatiya Janata Party national president Nitin Nabin is expected to undertake a whirlwind tour of the state, beginning with western Uttar Pradesh, possibly next week close on the heels of national general secretary (organisation) BL Santhosh and state in-charge Vinod Tawde concluding their two-day Lucknow visit on Saturday after a series of organisational meetings. The back-to-back visits by the party’s top organisational leadership come as the BJP steps up preparations for the 2027 assembly elections and seeks to get a clear picture of its position on the ground through a combination of organisational certification, feedback from voters as well as workers and direct interaction with the cadre. Nabin’s western UP tour is likely to be the first leg of the wider exercise under which he is expected to visit all six organisational regions of the party —Awadh, Kanpur-Bundelkhand, Braj, Paschim (west), Kashi and Goraksh regions — one by one. While his programme is yet to be formally announced, party functionaries said the national president was likely to hold meetings with state and regional leaders as well as grassroots workers to take stock of the organisation and the political situation. “Earleir, the national president was expected to begin his western UP tour from September 12 but that did not materialise. Now, we expect him to come any day this month only, of course after pre-announcement of the rescheduled programme,” said Ashok Katariya, a senior BJP leader from western UP and member of Legislative Council, over the phone. The exercise, according to observers, assumes significance because the BJP is not relying merely on reports from its organisational units. Recently, it completed a statewide verification campaign to establish whether its grassroots machinery is active on the ground or exists only on paper. “We have verified 1.56 lakh of the total 1,77,516 booths and all 1,918 zonal executive committees. Most of the around 32,000 Shakti Kendras have also been verified,” BJP general secretary Deepak Patel, who headed the verification campaign, said. The verification exercise also threw up some gaps in the party’s ground network. Patel said around 7-8% of office bearers were found to be either inactive or non-existent because of reasons such as death, migration and these positions have been filled by new functionaries. “Now, the verification reports will be submitted to us through district presidents, enabling the party to make the next strategy,” he said. The feedback exercise is not confined to the party organisation. Senior BJP office bearers have also begun travelling to districts, combining the task of highlighting the Modi and Yogi governments’ achievements and welfare schemes with collecting feedback from voters and local party workers. “We maintain a diary where we note down the public feedback that we share with our state president and general secretary (organisation),” said a senior BJP leader currently touring an eastern UP district. “The exercise could provide a fair idea of the party’s standing when it is conscious of the political risks associated with prolonged incumbency,” he added. Another BJP leader currently in eastern UP said the concern was not merely about the voter sentiment after 10 years of incumbency but also about the state of morale of the cadre. The feedback gathered through ‘pravas’, coupled with the booth-level verification, is expected to be discussed during Nabin’s meetings. Meanwhile, the BJP is also gearing up for a fortnight-long outreach campaign beginning September 17, coinciding with the birthday of Prime Minister Narendra Modi. The ‘Seva Pakhwada’ campaign will be used as an opportunity before the polls to expand contact with people and showcase the good works of the Modi and Yogi governments while countering the Opposition’s narrative. Brajendra K Parashar is a Senior Journalist with the Hindustan Times, based in Lucknow, with nearly three decades of experience covering governance, public policy, politics and development in Uttar Pradesh. Over the years, he has reported extensively on key sectors, including energy and renewable power, mobility and transport, road safety, agriculture and allied sectors and issues related to farmers, rural development, taxation under the Goods and Services Tax (GST) and public administration. A seasoned political correspondent, Parashar closely tracks the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) and has covered every major election in Uttar Pradesh right from three-tier panchayat elections and urban local body polls to Assembly and Lok Sabha elections. He also reports regularly on the proceedings of the Uttar Pradesh Legislature, bureaucracy, governance, policy decisions and administrative developments with focus on their impact on public life. His reporting is known for its strong analytical approach, extensive use of official data. His areas of interests include investigative journalism, long-form political and policy analysis, data-driven reporting, elections and institutional reforms. Parashar holds a postgraduate degree in Political Science with First Division from Aligarh Muslim University (AMU), followed by a Diploma in Journalism and Mass Communication from the same university. His inclination towards journalism began during his student days, when he regularly contributed letters to editors and articles to newspapers and magazines. In the mid-1990S, his essay, “Should India Switch Over to the Presidential Form Of Government?”, published in Politics India magazine edited by noted constitutional expert Subhash C Kashyap, was adjudged the best entry in a national competition. His work has received professional recognition, including the Hindustan Times Journalist of the Month Award for an impactful series on drinking water issues during the 2010 Lok Sabha election campaign. Originally from Kasganj in western Uttar Pradesh, Parashar is currently based in Lucknow where continues to report on politics, governance and public policy. Read More

title: Only Roland Garros towel left, says Ukraine tennis player after Russian strike hits flat
teaser: Dayana Yastremska says her flat took a "direct hit" by a Russian missile in Odesa, and all that left was her Roland Garros towel.
description: Dayana Yastremska says her flat took a "direct hit" by a Russian missile in Odesa, and all that left was her Roland Garros towel.
content: Only Roland Garros towel left, says Ukraine tennis player after Russian strike hits flat 34 minutes ago Share Save Add as preferred on Google Jaroslav Lukiv DSNS / Odesa region Dayana Yastremska said her family's apartment was destroyed in "a direct hit by a Kalibr cruise missile" fired by Russia Ukrainian tennis player Dayana Yastremska has said her family's flat has been destroyed in a Russian aerial strike on the Black Sea port of Odesa. "This is what the 'Russian world' looks like. A direct hit by a Kalibr cruise missile," she wrote on social media, showing a photo of a burning multi-storey residential building. "The only thing that survived was a Roland Garros... towel," the 26-year-old added, posting an image of a famous clay orange towel from Paris's Grand Slam tournament hanging from the wreckage. Odesa regional head Oleh Kiper said 37 people were injured, including a baby, and two missing in the missile and drone attack on Odesa and nearby Chornomorsk on Friday night. Dayana Yastremska / Facebook Yastremska posted a photo of a signature orange clay Roland Garros towel from last year's tournament hanging from the wreckage of her apartment "A Russian missile destroyed our apartment in Odesa... SYMBOLIC. A piece of world tennis survived a Russian missile. Our home did not," Yastremska wrote on Instagram on Saturday. "@wta @itf_reviews Look at these images through our eyes," she said in a reference to the governing bodies of world tennis - the Women's Tennis Association and the International Tennis Federation. Yastremska - who in 2024 reached the semifinal stage of the Australian Open - is currently 113th in the women's world singles rankings. It is not the first time Ukrainian athletes' homes have been hit by Russia since the start of the full-scale invasion of Ukraine in 2022. Last year, Ukraine international football midfielder Heorhiy Sudakov said his flat in the capital Kyiv had been severely damaged by a Russian drone while his wife and child were at home. USTA via Getty Images Dayana Yastremska competed at this year's US Open in New York, losing in the first round War in Ukraine Drones Europe Ukraine

title: 100 years later, Iowa book that made Ruth Suckow famous is being revived
teaser: Ruth Suckow's remarkable collection 'Iowa Interiors' returns in a special centennial edition, featuring captivating new illustrations by talented artist Claudia McGehee. To complement the reissue, the Hearst Center hosts an exhibition spotl
description: Ruth Suckow's remarkable collection 'Iowa Interiors' returns in a special centennial edition, featuring captivating new illustrations by talented artist Claudia McGehee. To complement the reissue, the Hearst Center hosts an exhibition spotl
content: In 1926, Iowa writer Ruth Suckow published Iowa Interiors, a collection of 14 short stories drawn from the lives of people in the state’s farms and small towns. A century later, the book is returning to print in a new centennial edition from Cedar Falls-based Final Thursday Press, with new illustrations by Iowa artist Claudia McGehee. The Hearst Center for the Arts in Cedar Falls is marking the anniversary with an exhibition of McGehee’s original illustrations, running September 10 through December 6. The exhibition is part of a broader effort to bring Suckow’s work back to readers. Suckow was already an established writer when Iowa Interiors appeared. Her first novel, Country People, had been published in 1924, followed by The Odyssey of a Nice Girl in 1925. Iowa Interiors, published by Alfred A. Knopf, further established her reputation and has since become one of the works most closely associated with her portrayals of Iowa life.The beekeeper who became a chronicler of IowaBefore her literary career fully took hold, Suckow had an unusual occupation for a writer: beekeeping. She spent years in Earlville, Iowa, where she managed the Orchard Apiary. A 1930 Time profile described her as the manager-owner of the apiary, which she operated for six years. Suckow’s connection with Earlville would become an important part of her life and literary history.Her fiction focused on the people she observed around her, farmers, families, renters, ministers and residents of small communities. Iowa Interiors contains stories such as “A Start in Life,” “A Homecoming,” “Uprooted,” “Renters” and “A Rural Community,” depicting the pressures and changes shaping everyday life in early 20th-century Iowa. The complete original collection runs 283 pages. The Hearst Center describes the 1926 collection as the work that established Suckow’s national reputation.A century-old book gets another lifeFor today’s readers, one obstacle has been finding Suckow’s books in the first place. The Ruth Suckow Memorial Association says copies of Iowa Interiors have become increasingly difficult to find. The association has made many of the original stories available online while preparing for the new edition.The centennial edition is intended to change that. Final Thursday Press is publishing the new volume, edited by Julie Husband and Jim O’Loughlin. It will include a new introduction as well as illustrations commissioned from Claudia McGehee, whose work is being displayed at the Hearst Center alongside the anniversary celebration.McGehee has created 14 scratchboard illustrations, one for each story in the collection. The exhibition gives visitors a chance to see the original artwork while revisiting the world Suckow captured a century ago.Why Iowa Interiors still mattersSuckow’s Iowa was markedly different from the state of 2026. Her stories emerged from a world of small farms, village communities and economic constraints, rather than the large-scale agricultural landscape that dominates much of Iowa today. But the subjects of her fiction are less distant: people trying to make a living, maintain families, find independence and adjust to communities changing around them.That is part of what the editors of the new edition hope readers will rediscover. Rather than treating Iowa Interiors simply as a historical record, the centennial project presents it as literature that can still speak to contemporary readers. A century after its first publication, the book is therefore returning to the place and literary tradition that shaped it, giving a new generation a chance to meet the Iowa that Suckow saw, one ordinary life at a time.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. Knopf, further established her reputation and has since become one of the works most closely associated with her portrayals of Iowa life.The beekeeper who became a chronicler of IowaBefore her literary career fully took hold, Suckow had an unusual occupation for a writer: beekeeping. She spent years in Earlville, Iowa, where she managed the Orchard Apiary. A 1930 Time profile described her as the manager-owner of the apiary, which she operated for six years. Suckow’s connection with Earlville would become an important part of her life and literary history.Her fiction focused on the people she observed around her, farmers, families, renters, ministers and residents of small communities. Iowa Interiors contains stories such as “A Start in Life,” “A Homecoming,” “Uprooted,” “Renters” and “A Rural Community,” depicting the pressures and changes shaping everyday life in early 20th-century Iowa. The complete original collection runs 283 pages. The Hearst Center describes the 1926 collection as the work that established Suckow’s national reputation.A century-old book gets another lifeFor today’s readers, one obstacle has been finding Suckow’s books in the first place. The Ruth Suckow Memorial Association says copies of Iowa Interiors have become increasingly difficult to find. The association has made many of the original stories available online while preparing for the new edition.The centennial edition is intended to change that. Final Thursday Press is publishing the new volume, edited by Julie Husband and Jim O’Loughlin. It will include a new introduction as well as illustrations commissioned from Claudia McGehee, whose work is being displayed at the Hearst Center alongside the anniversary celebration.McGehee has created 14 scratchboard illustrations, one for each story in the collection. The exhibition gives visitors a chance to see the original artwork while revisiting the world Suckow captured a century ago.Why Iowa Interiors still mattersSuckow’s Iowa was markedly different from the state of 2026. Her stories emerged from a world of small farms, village communities and economic constraints, rather than the large-scale agricultural landscape that dominates much of Iowa today. But the subjects of her fiction are less distant: people trying to make a living, maintain families, find independence and adjust to communities changing around them.That is part of what the editors of the new edition hope readers will rediscover. Rather than treating Iowa Interiors simply as a historical record, the centennial project presents it as literature that can still speak to contemporary readers. A century after its first publication, the book is therefore returning to the place and literary tradition that shaped it, giving a new generation a chance to meet the Iowa that Suckow saw, one ordinary life at a time.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. title: MPTBC Awaits Over INR 300 Crore Dues For Free Study Material Supply Across Madhya Pradesh
teaser: Bhopal (Madhya Pradesh): The Madhya Pradesh Text Book Corporation (MPTBC) supplies free study material and other educational material to the Rajya Shiksha Kendra and the Directorate of Public Instruction. Dues from the two agencies have rem
description: Bhopal (Madhya Pradesh): The Madhya Pradesh Text Book Corporation (MPTBC) supplies free study material and other educational material to the Rajya Shiksha Kendra and the Directorate of Public Instruction. Dues from the two agencies have rem
content: Bhopal (Madhya Pradesh): The Madhya Pradesh Text Book Corporation (MPTBC) supplies free study material and other educational material to the Rajya Shiksha Kendra and the Directorate of Public Instruction. Dues from the two agencies have remained pending for several years and stand at Rs 300,18,65,146. The delay has blocked the corporation's funds and caused loss of interest, according to its audit report for financial year 2024-25. Loss of Rs 57 lakh due to unsaleable, useless books On the basis of audit report received from various depots and information related to physical verification and inspection of depots, it came to fore that total 1,02,900 books were found unsaleable, obsolete and useless. The net sale price of them was Rs 57,68,185. At the same time, Corporation has to bear various expenditure on the storage and maintenance of these books. The expenditure includes godown rent, electricity expenditure, labour and other expenditures. Had these books were sold timely, then corporation would not have suffered the loss of Rs 57,68,185, said the audit report. title: 'Global South must shape, not just follow, rules': PM Modi at Brics Summit
teaser: Prime Minister Modi opened the Brics summit, demanding urgent United Nations Security Council reforms. He stressed transforming global governance from privilege to partnership for developing nations. Modi proposed Brics draft ten proposals
description: Prime Minister Modi opened the Brics summit, demanding urgent United Nations Security Council reforms. He stressed transforming global governance from privilege to partnership for developing nations. Modi proposed Brics draft ten proposals
content: NEW DELHI: Declaring the 18th Brics leaders' summit open, PM Narendra Modi stressed that UN Security Council (UNSC) reforms cannot be delayed any longer and that the "pyramid of privilege" reflected in the current global governance structure must be transformed into a "platform of partnership".Modi focused on economic integration of the Global South in his address at the session on inclusive governance and multilateralism, saying the bloc must work together to turn developing countries from rule-takers to rule-shapers."The Global South today stands in the front row of global crises, but in the back row of decision-making," the PM said, proposing that Brics draft 10 proposals for global governance reform.Modi positions Brics as an inclusive, not anti-west, forumThese should be focused on representation, responsiveness and rulemaking, PM Modi said. He sought a system “where every country has a voice, every member has a stake and the development of humanity remains at the centre of all endeavours”.On representation, he said UNSC reform can no longer be delayed and text-based negotiations on this subject must be tied to a fixed timeline and clear outcomes. “Similarly, voting power, leadership positions and policy priorities within global financial institutions must reflect today’s economic realities. Countries driving global economic growth deserve an appropriate role in shaping global economic governance,” he added.While western experts have often described Brics as an anti-West forum, Modi said the grouping operates not against anyone, but with an inclusive approach that brings everyone along. “Today, Brics is also in its coming-of-age moment. Over the past 20 years, Brics has established a distinct identity on the global stage. We respect each other’s perspectives and move forward through consensus,” he said.The PM called upon the bloc to work on an ambitious new agenda, translating its unity and consensus into concrete results on the global stage. He proposed establishment of a Brics Continuity and Implementation Mechanism. “Brics presidency changes every year, but this should not disrupt our institutional momentum. Under this mechanism, all initiatives and outcomes can be followed up through the troika (past, current and incoming presidency),” said Modi.Raising the issue of seafarers’ safety, Modi talked about how they make a massive contribution to global trade and yet lack adequate support in difficult times. He proposed creating a Seafarers Emergency Support Network to connect maritime authorities and missions of relevant nations. “This network would assist with distress alerts, medical aid, family notifications and evacuation efforts.”He said ensuring equal participation in setting the global rules of the future is critical. “AI, cyberspace, outer space, biotechnology and critical technologies are shaping not only future opportunities, but also future rules. We must work to transform the Global South from rule-takers to rule-shapers,” he said. “The message of this Brics summit must be clear: if our future is shared, the right to shape it must also be shared,” he said.Get the latest India News and Live updates.
